prs.title: RBAC R3a: identity routes on the authorization evaluator + role configuration UI
prs.body:
## Summary

RBAC R3a: users, organizations, roles and role assignments now decide access with the role and permission model through the authorization evaluator, and the UI follows what the signed-in person can actually do.

**Live access change at merge: none for existing accounts.** Nobody holds Platform Operator or any identity permission today. Platform Admins keep everything. Users, External users, provider-organization members and workflow engine tokens get the same decisions as before. Engine and service tokens keep their current decision on identity routes until R3b gives them a typed principal.

### What's in it
- **Backend:** the identity routes are decided by `src.services.authorization.enforce` at the target's organization. A user holding any privileged permission is *protected*: only a Platform Admin may change them. Non-admins can grant only roles with no permissions. Every role assignment now records its boundary, and a backfill migration adds home-organization boundaries to existing assignments. 42 of 748 access-catalog entries are on the evaluator.
- **New endpoints:** `GET /auth/authorization` (the caller's effective grants), `GET|PUT /api/users/{id}/role-assignments`, `GET|PUT /api/roles/{id}/permissions` (identity permissions only), and `POST /api/users/{id}/mfa/reset`.
- **Platform Admin is an additional role, not a base role.** Every user's base role is User or a custom role (a custom base can lower permissions further). Platform Admin is held as an additional role that applies everywhere; only a Platform Admin can grant or remove it, and only to provider-organization or Global users. A migration moves today's admins to base User plus a Platform Admin assignment; `is_superuser` is unchanged for everyone.
- **Permissions resolve from one effective list.** A person's grants are (permission, boundary) pairs: the base role at their home organization plus each additional role at its boundaries. Platform Admin's wildcard (`*`) is stored as its role permission like any other; "is Platform Admin" means holding `*` at the platform boundary. No custom role can be given `*`, and `*` still excludes `secrets.read`. A structural test keeps role-identity checks out of permission resolution.
- **Platform Operator is for provider-organization people only.** It can't be given to anyone outside the provider organization, and a user who holds it can't be moved out of the provider organization; remove Operator first. This applies to single and bulk moves.
- **Reset MFA** removes the user's authenticator app, recovery codes, passkeys and remembered devices, and signs them out everywhere. They enroll again at their next password sign-in. It is audited (`user.mfa_reset`, counts only). It refuses with 409 a user who has no password and no linked SSO account but has a passkey, because they would be left with no way to sign in. You can't reset your own account here; use Security settings.
- **UI:** a Roles & access section in the user dialog; role detail pages show built-in roles and edit identity permissions; a People tab on the Platform Operator and Secrets Reader pages; organization and user actions gated by permission. The users row menu gains Reset MFA and Sign out of all devices.
- **Migrations:** `20261001_r3a_boundary_fill` → `20261001_r3a_operator_desc` → `20261002_r3a_admin_additional` (after `20261001_unified_file_search`), each with a rehearsal test. Single head checked against current main.

### Who can do what after this PR

| Action | Rule after this PR | Platform Operator (customer orgs) |
|---|---|---|
| List and view users | `users.read` where the user belongs; lists filtered | yes |
| Invite an ordinary user | `users.readwrite` in that organization | yes (new: was admin-only) |
| Change name, enable or disable, reset MFA, resend or revoke an invite, sign out of all devices | `users.readwrite`; protected accounts admin-only | yes |
| Move, delete, change email or base role | `users.lifecycle.readwrite`; Platform Admin changes admin-only | no |
| Assign additional roles | `roleassignments.readwrite`; non-admins only roles with no permissions, never on protected accounts | permission-free roles only |
| View organizations | `organizations.read`; filtered | customer orgs |
| Create, edit, disable organizations | `organizations.readwrite` | no |
| Create or edit roles and their permissions | `roles.readwrite` platform-wide | no |

Stricter than before, by design: a demoted admin loses identity access immediately instead of at token expiry. Bulk role replacement never adds built-in roles and leaves built-in roles a user already holds (Platform Admin, Platform Operator) as they are; it manages custom roles only.

**Known limits:** bulk "Replace roles" needs role-list access, so Operators assign roles per user. Moving a user to another organization leaves their additional-role placements where they were (same as today). Secrets Reader stays unassignable until R3b. `PATCH /api/users/{id}` with `mfa_enabled=false` still exists as a flag flip; the UI uses the real reset.

## Test plan

Run locally against this worktree's test stack, after merging current main:
- [x] Full backend unit suite: 8080 passed (after merging main through #882)
- [x] Full client unit suite: 536 files, 3349 tests passed
- [x] `./test.sh quality api`: pyright 0 errors, ruff clean
- [x] Backend unit (425 passed): `test_access_list`, `test_alembic_single_head`, `test_builtin_roles`, `test_contract_version`, `test_dto_flags`, `test_identity_authorization`, `test_mcp_thin_wrapper`, `test_user_mfa_reset`, `tests/unit/authorization/` (incl. `test_decision_matrix`), `services/test_operation_catalog`, `sdk/test_sdk_users_service`, `sdk/test_set_user_base_role`, `test_is_superuser_single_writer`, `test_datetime_consistency`
- [x] Backend e2e (125 passed on the final head, incl. every migration rehearsal; 136 on the earlier head): `api/test_auth`, `test_organizations`, `test_roles*`, `test_users*`, `platform/test_r3a_identity_authorization`, the three R3a migration rehearsals, `test_authorization_deny_probe`, `test_external_users`, `test_cli_roles`, `test_cli_orgs`

- [x] Client: `npm run tsc` clean; `npm run lint` 0 errors (5 warnings in untouched files); vitest 185 passed across the 19 changed test files

prs.body:
## Summary

Test-only. Adds `api/tests/e2e/scenarios/`, one e2e module that records how workflow runs are identified and which orgs they act in, for every way a run starts. It is the baseline later RBAC slices (Operator, record-only "started by", R3b managed identities) are checked against. No product code changes.

- **World** (module-scoped): Contoso/Fabrikam/provider personas plus HR (permission-free role), external and custom-base-role users; one observation table per partition; an integration with a mapping per org; global config with a Contoso override and a secret.
- **Probe workflow** in four homes (provider, Contoso, global, new global). One run tries every scope knob (`set_scope`, `tables.insert/upsert/query` with `scope=`, `config.get`, `integrations.get`, raw `bifrost.api`, the context's scope set directly) against Contoso, Fabrikam, provider and global, and can spawn children (depth 2, `run_as`).
- **Starts**: REST, request `org_id`, direct web-SDK table reads, form submit, chat tool call (in-process test model), delayed (`delay_seconds` + in-process promoter), webhook (signed and unsigned; provider, global and Contoso sources), schedule (in-process tick on a frozen clock), topic, endpoint key.
- **Checks**: write effects are read back from the tables as admin, not taken from the probe's own report. Each start's cells are compared with the managed-identity model in `rule.py`, except cells listed in `pre_r3b.py` ("pre-MI behaviour (R3b)"), which record today's value. `test_pre_r3b_entries_are_live` fails once an entry matches the model, so the table can only shrink. Separate invariant tests (customers stay in their org, unattended Contoso workflows stay in Contoso, refused writes leave no row, children stay within the starter's reach) are computed straight from the observations.
- **Journeys** J1–J8: role-gated onboarding with a `run_as` child; the same onboarding aimed at another customer is refused; staff onboard a customer; an unattended dispatcher replays a stored request as its submitter; provider fleet job; global job switching to the provider org; app-style table reads; config, secret and mapping fallback. They hold today and must hold unchanged after R3b.

## Cost

Starting with the authoring rules for expensive e2e tests: there are about 42 worker executions, all launched together and then polled together. The world plus every run takes **25.3 s** (`scenario_runs_seconds` suite property). The module's summed case time is 43.5 s, including session persona setup, and almost all of it is the first test's fixture setup. Each execution is one entry point × identity combination, a cross-process contract that can't be observed below the worker. Edge cases stay as cells inside one run instead of adding jobs.

prs.title: fix(websocket): table subscribe uses the REST target-org rule
prs.body:
## Summary

When a provider-org member (not a platform admin) opened an app table with `useTable(..., { scope: <customer org> })`, they saw **"Table not found"** instead of rows.
- The REST query (`/api/tables/{name}/documents/query?scope=<org>`) returned 200 with the right rows.
- The realtime subscribe for the same table (`table:<uuid>` over the WebSocket) was answered `{"type":"error","message":"Table not found"}`, and the hook showed that error instead of the rows.

**Cause:** the UUID branch of `_resolve_table_id` in `api/src/routers/websocket.py` allowed only superusers to reach tables outside their own org. REST resolves the target org through `resolve_target_org`, which also lets provider-org members in, per the canonical rule in `repositories/README.md`.

**Fix:** subscribing to a table in another org now goes through `resolve_target_org`, so the WebSocket and REST make the same decision. A plain member of another org is still refused.

## Verification

- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_websocket_table_resolution.py tests/e2e/platform/test_subscriptions.py -v` → 17 passed. This includes three new UUID-branch tests (other-org member refused, provider member allowed, superuser allowed) and the existing `test_subscribe_to_other_org_table_rejected`.
- The new provider test fails without the fix.
- `./test.sh quality api` → clean.
- Live check on a debug stack, with a provider member using an app with a scope picker:
  - Before: `subscribe` → `error: Table not found`.
  - After: `subscribed` for both customer tables, and the rows render.

prs.title: Platform Operator for provider staff; Secrets Reader for Platform Admins
prs.body:
## Summary

This is the follow-up to #879. Platform Operator becomes the role provider-organization staff use to support customer organizations, and Platform Admins receive Secrets Reader before R3b starts enforcing it.

- **Platform Operator gains `workflows.execute`**, so staff can run workflows (onboarding, for example) in customer organizations once R3b enforces execution. Its description says so.
- **A migration (`20261003_r3_operator_secrets`) assigns Platform Operator** at "all customer organizations" to every existing provider-organization member who is not a Platform Admin, a system account or an external user (inactive members included). Assignments that already exist keep their own boundaries. New users get nothing automatically.
- **The same migration assigns Secrets Reader** to every Platform Admin who is not a system account, at platform + all customer organizations + the provider organization. It has no effect until `secrets.read` is enforced. A Platform Admin can now assign or remove Secrets Reader, with those fixed boundaries and no picker.
- **`/auth/authorization` returns a Platform Admin's own grants** (`*` at platform, plus Secrets Reader), so Roles & access shows them.
- The downgrade removes only the rows this migration created.

## Before / after

**Provider-organization staff who exist at migration time.** Membership in the provider organization alone grants nothing on the routes already decided by the authorization evaluator, so these routes return 403 for staff today.

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Users list/detail | 403 | Customer-organization users (provider org and Global still 403) |
| Invite/create, invite resend/regenerate/revoke, MFA reset, session revoke, (de)activate | 403 | Ordinary (non-protected) users in customer organizations |
| Organizations list/detail | 403 | Customer organizations readable; create/update/delete and the provider org still 403 |
| Role assignments, role users | 403 | Read in customer organizations; assign only roles that carry no permissions, to ordinary users |
| Sidebar | No Organizations / Users | Both visible |
| Protected account | No | Yes (only Platform Admins can act on them) |
| Moving them out of the provider org | Allowed | 409 until Platform Operator is removed (existing Operator rule) |
| `workflows.execute` | — | Held; not yet enforced, so no change in how they run workflows |

**Everyone else**

|---|---|---|
| Platform Admins (human) | No Secrets Reader | Hold Secrets Reader (no access change until enforcement); shown in Roles & access and on the role's People tab |
| Platform Admin assigning Secrets Reader | 409 "can't be assigned yet" | Allowed, fixed boundaries |
| System accounts, external users, customer users, new users | — | Unchanged |

prs.title: Identities: default per organization, global, and the workflow's unattended identity
prs.body:
## Summary

Identities are ordinary user accounts that run work no person started (schedules, webhooks, events, endpoint keys). This change creates them and lets a workflow name the one it runs unattended as. **Nothing runs as an identity yet** — run lineage (next change) reads them.

- **`users.identity_kind`** marks an identity: `org_default` (one per organization, including the provider organization), `global_default` (one, with no organization) or `custom` (for later). Identities take role assignments like anyone else.
- **Migration `20261003_r3b_identities`** creates a default identity for every organization and the global identity (the users organization check is widened to allow it), and gives the provider organization's identity **Platform Admin** through an ordinary assignment. Every global workflow with an event subscription or an enabled endpoint gets `run_identity_id` = the provider organization's identity, which matches how those runs are treated today. Idempotent; the downgrade removes exactly what it created.
- **Creating an organization** — through the API or a git-sync import — creates its default identity in the same transaction.
- **Identities never sign in.** Every path that mints session tokens (password, MFA, passkey, device code, refresh, SSO, MCP OAuth) refuses them; SSO provisioning, registration and user creation refuse the reserved `identities.bifrost.internal` email domain.
- **Identities stay out of people management:** not in the Users list, user counts or first-user detection; update/delete through the people routes answer 409, bulk operations report them as per-user failures.
- **`workflows.run_identity_id`** (PATCH, CLI `--run-identity-id`, MCP `run_identity_id`, workflow response): an identity of the workflow's own organization; for a global or provider-organization workflow, the global identity or a provider-organization identity. Null = the organization's default identity. Every write that changes a workflow's organization (PATCH, re-registration, git-sync pull) re-checks it. It is environment-specific and not written to the manifest; git-sync and deploy leave it in place.
- **`users.organization_id` now follows its organization's id** (`ON UPDATE CASCADE`), so git sync can still re-key an organization matched by name across environments now that every organization has an account.

## Before / after

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Any workflow, form, app, agent or trigger run | — | Unchanged (scenario matrix unchanged, `pre_r3b.py` untouched) |
| Users list, counts, first-user setup | — | Unchanged (identities excluded) |
| Organizations | No accounts created | Each has a default identity, created with it |
| Platform Admin role holders | People only | Also the provider organization's identity (shows on the role's People tab) |
| Global workflows with a subscription or enabled endpoint | — | Name the provider organization's identity (`run_identity_id`; not read yet) |
| Sign-in / register with an identity email | — | 401 |
| Create a person on `@identities.bifrost.internal` | Allowed | 422 |
| PATCH / delete an identity via `/api/users/{id}` | — | 409 "Identities are managed from Identities" |
| Git sync re-keying an organization matched by name | Refused when the organization had any account | Its accounts follow it |

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `./test.sh quality api` | clean |
| `./test.sh unit` (full; contract fingerprint refreshed for the additive field) | 8096 passed |
| `./test.sh e2e` (full backend, before review fixes) | 2119 passed, 1 error (round-trip cleanup — fixed in this PR) |
| After review fixes: git sync, round-trip, workspace bundle import, workflows, organizations, auth, users, identity/run-identity tests, scenario matrix, all migration rehearsals | green |
| `client`: `npm run tsc`, `npm run lint`; `v1.d.ts` regenerated | clean |
| Debug-stack drive (CLI + REST): new organization gets its identity; Users list has none; identity sign-in/register refused; reserved domain refused; `bifrost workflows update --run-identity-id` sets an allowed identity and refuses a disallowed one | as expected |

New tests: `test_r3b_identities_migration_rehearsal.py`, `test_identities_service.py`, `test_identity_accounts.py`, `test_workflow_run_identity.py`, plus git-sync organization/workflow import cases.

## Post-deploy check

Identity count per organization (one each, plus one global); provider identity holds Platform Admin; count of global workflows naming it; every identity's `last_login` is NULL; API error classes unchanged.

prs.title: Runs record who they run for: run user, starter and root execution
prs.body:
## Summary

Every run now records who it runs for. Each execution gets `run_user_id`, `started_by_user_id` and `root_execution_id`; each agent run gets `run_user_id`. **Nothing reads these for a decision yet**: authorization, scope, the SDK-visible identity (`context.user_id`, `is_platform_admin`), `executed_by` and error behaviour are unchanged. The next change observes against them.

- **One module decides lineage** where a run starts: `shared/run_lineage.py`.
  - A person (REST, CLI, web SDK, app, form, data provider, MCP, chat, integration test run, delayed run): the person. An admin's `run_as` changes the acting user, not the run user.
  - A child run (engine token): copied from the parent execution, so a whole tree keeps the starter's user and the first run's id as root. A parent that recorded no lineage (started before deploy) gives its child none.
  - Schedule, webhook, topic, endpoint key: the workflow's `run_identity_id`, otherwise its organization's default identity; a global workflow uses the global identity.
  - Anonymous or embedded form/app, service: the default identity of that form's or app's organization (global identity when it has none).
- **Transport.** Every enqueue/run function takes a required keyword-only `lineage`. The pending record carries it to the consumer, which writes it on the row. The engine token gets attribution-only claims (`engine_run_user_id`, `engine_started_by_user_id`, `engine_root_execution_id`). Delayed rows store it at insert and the promoter forwards it. A pending record written before deploy (no `lineage` key) is consumed as before, with no lineage recorded.
- **Agent runs** record their run user:
  - API, rerun, chat, SDK and MCP gateway runs: the caller.
  - Event-started runs: the agent organization's identity.
  - Delegated runs: the delegating run's user.
  - Workflow tool calls run for the agent run's user.
- **Migration `20261004_r3b_lineage`**:
  - Nullable columns with no defaults; existing rows stay NULL.
  - Foreign keys `ON DELETE SET NULL` added `NOT VALID`, so adding them doesn't scan the 4 GB `executions` table.
  - Partial indexes (`IS NOT NULL`) built `CONCURRENTLY`, so deleting a user doesn't scan `executions`.
- **Also included:**
  - `IdentityKind` moves to `src.models.enums`, so the worker and scheduler import lineage without fastapi.
  - The webhook protocol imports starlette's `Request` for typing only. This fixes `test_import_hygiene::test_scheduler_closure_has_no_heavyweights`, which already failed on main; it is slow-marked, so the PR lane doesn't run it.
  - The scenario matrix gains `test_every_run_records_its_lineage`, and its world gives the global probe the provider organization's identity, as the identities migration does.

## Before / after

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Any run's behaviour, access, scope, SDK identity, `executed_by` | — | Unchanged (scenario matrix unchanged, `pre_r3b.py` untouched) |
| `executions` row | `executed_by` only | + run user, starter, root execution |
| `agent_runs` row | `caller_user_id` (string) | + `run_user_id` |
| Engine token | `engine_caller_*` attribution | + `engine_run_user_id`, `engine_started_by_user_id`, `engine_root_execution_id` (attribution only) |
| Deleting a user | Nulls `executed_by` (indexed) | Also nulls the lineage columns (partial indexes) |

## Not in this change

- No `cause_user_id`. Events don't record who emitted them yet; that capture and the column come with the observers.
- No backfill. Existing rows, including the delayed row pending in production, keep NULL lineage.
- Agent system tools that call the REST API through the MCP bridge record that token's account. That is the caller when a person started the agent, and the system account for event-started agent runs. Carrying the agent run's identity through the bridge needs a principal claim reader, which comes with the observers.
- `rule.REACH` / `pre_r3b.py` are unchanged; the reach expectations move with the observers.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `./test.sh quality api` | 0 errors, ruff clean |
| `./test.sh unit` | 8124 passed |
| `./test.sh e2e` (full, before the final review fixes) | 2125 passed |
| After the review fixes: `tests/e2e/scenarios/`, `test_agent_delegation_lifecycle.py`, `test_run_lineage_anonymous.py`, `test_mcp_endpoints.py`, `test_r3b_lineage_migration_rehearsal.py`, `tests/unit/services/mcp_server/` | all passed |
| `tests/unit/test_import_hygiene.py` (slow) | 4 passed |
| Matrix mutation (child lineage removed) | `test_every_run_records_its_lineage` fails on every child and grandchild |

prs.title: Ship the V2 scaffold's starter button unwired
prs.body:
## Problem

The V2 App scaffold's starter "Run workflow" button called a sample workflow by default (`functions/hello.py::main` in a Solution, rewritten to `workflows/hello.py::main` for `bifrost app create`). An independent App's instance has no such workflow, so the first click returned 404.

## Change

One starter behaviour for both scaffolds:

- **App.tsx (shared by `bifrost solution scaffold-app`, `solution migrate-app`, and `bifrost app create`)**: the button is an unwired placeholder with no `onClick` and no workflow hook. The comment beside it explains `useWorkflowQuery` (read) and `useWorkflowMutation` (action), the portable `path::function` ref format, and shows the wired mutation pattern (mutate, disabled while loading, error, result). `bifrost` is imported for `BifrostHeader` only.
- **Solution scaffold**: no longer writes `functions/hello.py` or its `.bifrost/workflows.yaml` entry. The workflow existed only to back the button. Without a caller, every scaffolded Solution, and every `migrate-app` run since it shares `_scaffold_app`, would deploy an unused `hello` workflow into each install. Removed along with `_SAMPLE_WORKFLOW_*` and the "Sample workflow at ..." output.
- **App scaffold**: the App.tsx comment is now neutral, so `_scaffold` keeps only the start/deploy command and "V2 App" replacements. The four comment/ref replacements are gone; one of them already matched nothing.
- **Skill**: the `bifrost-migrate` step 2 description of App.tsx is updated, and the Codex mirror is synced (`scripts/sync-codex-skills.sh`). Plugin version is unchanged, per the release flow.

### Before
```tsx
const wf = useWorkflowMutation<{ message: string }>("functions/hello.py::main");
<button onClick={() => wf.mutate({})} disabled={wf.loading}>Run workflow</button>
```
plus `functions/hello.py` + a `workflows.yaml` entry in Solution workspaces.

### After
```tsx
// This button is a placeholder: wire it to one of your workflows.
// ...hook guidance + wired example...
<button type="button" className="...">Run workflow</button>
```
No sample workflow is written.

## Tests

- `test_solution_scaffold_app.py`: new `test_scaffold_app_starter_button_is_an_unwired_placeholder`, which checks that non-comment code has no `useWorkflow`/`onClick`, there is no `hello.py` ref, and the wiring guidance is present. The nav-shell test drops its mutation assertions. The nested-path test no longer expects `workflows.yaml`/`functions/hello.py`.
- `test_solution_scaffold_dev_wiring.py`: the sample-ref/sample-placement tests are replaced with `test_scaffold_app_writes_no_sample_workflow`, which checks for no `workflows.yaml`, no `functions/`, and no `.py` files.
- `test_cli_app.py`: the App scaffold's `App.tsx` must equal the Solution scaffold's, byte for byte.
- `test_solution_collect_python.py`: the docstring/comment no longer claims the scaffold writes `functions/hello.py`. The behaviour under test is unchanged.

Commands run:
- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_solution_scaffold_app.py tests/unit/test_cli_app.py tests/unit/test_solution_scaffold_dev_wiring.py tests/unit/test_solution_collect_python.py tests/unit/test_cli_solution_migrate_app.py tests/unit/test_skill_reference_freshness.py tests/unit/test_skill_cli_claims.py -v`: 24 passed
- `./test.sh quality api`: pyright 0 errors, ruff clean
- `python3 scripts/check_skill_mirrors.py`: mirrors fresh

Not run: full unit/e2e suites (merge queue), and no type-check of the generated TSX against the SDK. The change only removes the hook call and the import.

prs.title: App SDK header: one row with a menu button on phones, nav prop
prs.body:
## Summary

Two changes to `BifrostHeader` (the web SDK, `client/src/lib/app-sdk/bifrost-header.tsx`): it stays on one row on phones, and it can render the app's navigation through a new optional `nav` prop.

**Phones (below 640px).** The header is one row in the navigation-drawer layout (as in Gmail, GitHub and Material): a menu button on the left (`aria-label="Open menu"`, `aria-expanded`), then the truncated title, and nothing else. The button opens a panel under the header with:
- "Back to Bifrost" (first item; it leaves the bar on phones)
- the nav links
- the `action` slot
- the theme toggle (when `supportsTheme`)
- the account section: name, email, Log out

Without `nav`, the panel still holds Back to Bifrost, the theme toggle and the account section.

The panel is a full-width sheet hanging from the bar, not a full-height left drawer. At 390px a drawer would cover most of the screen anyway. The sheet keeps the bar visible, so the button in the top-left corner stays the close control (it shows an X). Its height fits its contents.

Accessibility and closing:
- The panel is `role="dialog"` labelled "Menu".
- Focus moves to its first control and Tab cycles inside it.
- Escape closes it and returns focus to the menu button.
- It also closes on a backdrop tap, on following a link, on browser back/forward, and when the viewport crosses the breakpoint.

The breakpoint is read with `matchMedia` (`useSyncExternalStore`), so phones never mount the wide controls. The `action` slot therefore renders in exactly one place.

**`nav` prop.** `nav={{ items: [{ label, to, end? }], link: NavLink }}`.
- The SDK stays router-free: its only peer dependencies are react, react-dom and lucide-react. The app passes its router's link component, and react-router's `NavLink` fits the `BifrostNavLinkProps` contract as-is. The vitest file passes the real `NavLink`, so tsc checks that.
- Active state comes from the `aria-current="page"` the router sets. The header's scoped stylesheet styles it: foreground text and underline on wide screens, an accent background on phones.
- New exported types: `BifrostHeaderNav`, `BifrostNavItem`, `BifrostNavLinkProps`.

**Desktop: the links render as a tab row inside the header, under the title bar, not inline in the bar.** Reasons:
- It keeps the #896 shell's look and still fits long titles and five or more sections (the row scrolls horizontally).
- Inline links would compete with the title and controls for one row and force a second truncation rule.
- The app has one nav list, and one component renders it at both widths.

**Scaffold.** `_v2_scaffold_files` `app_tsx`, which `bifrost app create` reuses, now passes `NAV` through `nav` instead of rendering its own `NavLink` row. The `cn` import was only used by that row, so it is gone. The scaffold tests are updated, rebased on #897.

**Docs.**
- The build skill's `best-practices/apps.md` and `references/web-sdk-v2.md` now describe the prop and the phone layout.
- `generated/web-sdk-surface.md` is regenerated.
- The mirrors are synced with `scripts/sync-codex-skills.sh`.

**Light-theme contrast.** I re-measured the "low contrast" I reported earlier on the active nav link and the primary button. Once the theme transition finishes, the computed colours are correct: foreground `oklch(0.145 0 0)` for the active link, `oklch(0.985 0 0)` text on `oklch(0.38 0.09 220)` for the button. My earlier screenshots were taken mid-way through the 0.12–0.15s colour transition after a theme toggle. There was nothing to fix, so no colours changed. The new screenshots wait for transitions to settle.

The change is compatible: `sdk-contract.json` is untouched and no SDK file was added, so the Dockerfile SDK lists are unchanged.

## Before / after

Measured on a deployed V2 App titled "Service Desk Operations Dashboard", headless Chromium, light and dark:

| Viewport | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| 390px | Two rows (82px): title, then theme toggle, avatar, name and chevron wrapped below; separate nav row under that | One row (46px): `☰  Service Desk Operations Dashboard` (the title truncates when longer); no nav row |
| 390px, menu open | — | Full-width panel (320px): ← Back to Bifrost · Home (active), About · Dark/Light mode · avatar, name, email · Log out; backdrop dims the page; focus on "Back to Bifrost"; tapping About goes to `/about` and closes the panel |
| 1280px | Title bar (51px) + the scaffold's own nav row | Same title bar + the header's tab row (90px total); Home underlined |

## Tests and checks

- `./test.sh client unit src/lib/app-sdk/bifrost-header.test.tsx`: 19 passed.
  - wide: one-row bar and title truncation; `nav` tab row with the active route marked
  - desktop: back link first in the bar
  - phone: the bar is exactly [menu button, title], with no links and no logo; panel contents in order (Back to Bifrost, nav links, action, theme, name/email, Log out)
  - focus moves into the panel and Tab stays inside it
  - Escape closes and returns focus; following a link closes and navigates; a backdrop tap closes
  - crossing the breakpoint closes the panel
  - without `nav`: theme and account only
  - happy-dom's real `matchMedia`/viewport is used for the breakpoint
- `(cd client && npm run tsc)`: clean. `(cd client && npm run lint)`: 0 errors; the 5 warnings are in other files.
- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_solution_scaffold_app.py tests/unit/test_cli_app.py tests/unit/test_solution_scaffold_dev_wiring.py tests/unit/test_cli_app_migrate.py tests/unit/test_migrate_v2.py tests/unit/test_sdk_package.py tests/unit/test_sdk_package_fingerprint.py`: 42 passed.
- `./test.sh quality api`: pyright 0 errors, ruff clean.
- Rebuilt-SDK check, on a port-mode debug stack built from this branch:
  - `/api/sdk/download` serves a tarball whose `dist/index.mjs` contains the new header; the peer dependencies are unchanged (react, react-dom, lucide-react).
  - `bifrost app deploy` of the new scaffold built and rendered.
  - `bifrost apps sdk status` shows `current`, fingerprint `a939c45aa5759324` (main's was `f2a847c21ef9b159`), contract version `2`.
  - Earlier on this PR, `bifrost apps sdk update` moved an existing App to the rebuilt SDK through the `application.sdk_update` job.

Not run: full client vitest, Playwright, backend unit/e2e suites.

prs.title: Compress encoded encrypted Solution backup payloads
prs.body:
Encrypted file payloads used explicit ZipInfo entries whose default ZIP_STORED overrode the enclosing archive's ZIP_DEFLATED setting. This retained Base64's storage overhead even for incompressible files. Both streamed and in-memory writers now deflate ciphertext while preserving chunk encryption, Zip64, and the existing restore format.

Two regression cases reproduced 512 KiB of high-entropy input becoming approximately 699 KiB of stored payload. They now verify compressed size below 110% of plaintext and matching decrypted size/SHA-256. The existing encrypted export journey verifies API and object-storage integration.

Validation (Docker, isolated worktree):

- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_solution_file_payload_compression.py tests/unit/test_solution_file_capture.py tests/unit/test_solution_export.py tests/unit/test_solution_zip_install.py -q` — 42 passed.
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/platform/test_solution_export_files.py::test_full_export_files_in_encrypted_tier -q` — 1 passed.
- `./test.sh quality api` — Pyright and Ruff passed.

Full backend and client suites were not run. Full archive import capacity and extraction/storage efficiency remain separate work.

prs.title: Report-only access checks in the audit log (R3b 2c)
prs.body:
Every run is now checked, report-only, against the managed-identity model: for each call a run makes, the server works out what the model would decide (the run user's reach, plus what the workflow adds) next to what today's code decides, and writes to the audit log everything Phase 2 enforcement could change: every call the model would block, every move into another organization, and every `run_as`, policy and secret decision. Allowed calls inside the run user's own organization or Global, and denials today's code already makes, are not written because enforcement cannot change them. **Nothing changes what any request does**; today's code still decides everything.

## What it records

`access.check` audit events, outcome `success` / `failure` (`failure` = the model would block it), `details.enforced = false`, with the run user, workflow, route, target and a step-by-step trace:

| Check | Written when |
|---|---|
| Org a call acts in (tables, config, integrations, knowledge, files, lists) | the model would block it, or it acts in another organization |
| Child run placement, `run_as` of another user | blocked, or always for `run_as` |
| Entry (an agent run nobody started opening a workflow or its agent) | the model would block it |
| Table and file policies (judged with the run user's own roles and claims; admin predicate = Platform Admin or Full workflow) | the model would block what today allows, or a policy decision is made |
| Secret reads (kind and name, never the value) | always |

Each decision is written once per run. Calls the engine makes without run lineage, and checks that cannot be judged, are written as `access.check_gap` with a reason. Judging happens after the response is sent; policy checks run in a savepoint; a failure in any of it is logged and never reaches the request.

## Also in this PR
- The principal reads the run-lineage claims; the MCP REST bridge carries the run user of an agent nobody started (its system-tool child runs no longer record the system account).
- `GET /api/audit?group_by=workflow|action|resource_type|outcome|user|organization` returns counts and the newest entry per group. **Access change:** holders of `roleassignments.read` (Platform Operators, at customer organizations) can read `access.check` events in the organizations that permission reaches; everything else in the audit log stays Platform Admin only.
- Identity matrix: Global is in every reach. PRE_R3B: 46 cells leave (now match the rule), 67 join (today's SDK refuses a customer run's explicit Global target), 233 → 254. A new test checks that blocking exactly what the checks flag yields the rule, per route. Scenario staff hold the Platform Operator role, as production staff do.

## Before / after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Request behaviour | — | unchanged |
| Audit log | no access checks | `access.check` / `access.check_gap` events for runs |
| `/api/audit` | Platform Admins | Platform Admins; Operators read access checks in their reach; `group_by` |
| Agent system-tool child runs (agent nobody started) | run user = system account | run user = the agent's organization identity |

## Tests
- Unit: `./test.sh unit` (8196 passed); `./test.sh quality api` clean; import hygiene (slow) 4/4.
- E2E: `./test.sh e2e` full suite; new `tests/e2e/api/test_access_check_contracts.py`, `tests/e2e/api/test_audit_access_checks.py`; `tests/e2e/scenarios/` incl. `test_access_checks_predict_the_rule` (mutation-checked).
- Contract tripwires: DTO / contract version / access list / decision matrix; client types regenerated, `npm run tsc` clean.

prs.title: Restore large encrypted Solution backups without extracted payload copies
prs.body:
Encrypted Solution backups hit the ordinary source archive limits before restoration: the largest migrated Docs file is 268,313,994 bytes, exceeding the 128 MiB entry cap, and the full file set exceeds the 1 GiB extraction budget. Restore now reads encrypted payloads directly from ZIP members, without creating an extracted encrypted copy of every file.

Encrypted backups have separate bounded budgets: 32 GiB compressed archive/member limits and a 64 GiB aggregate uncompressed limit. Ordinary source bundles retain their 512 MiB compressed, 128 MiB entry and 1 GiB extracted limits. Install upload routes enforce their cap before multipart parsing. Payload reads bound headers, tokens and KDF memory; existing Fernet authentication and restored SHA256/size checks remain in place.

Preview and request-time validation inspect source/metadata only. The install job scans payload ZIP checksums with bounded reads before any install writes, so payload corruption becomes a failed job; corrupt source/metadata and wrong passwords still fail synchronously. Traversal, duplicate-member, entry-count and compression-ratio checks remain enforced.

Changed files:
- `api/src/main.py`
- `api/src/routers/solutions.py`
- `api/src/services/solutions/file_payloads.py`
- `api/src/services/solutions/zip_install.py`
- `api/tests/unit/routers/test_workspace_bundle_upload.py`
- `api/tests/unit/test_solution_backup_archive.py`
- `api/tests/unit/test_solution_zip_install.py`

Validation on candidate `32894ff007319b4f99acd10966928c90535f145c`, based on main `43f3f78d7f9b5b09dc3a7d0e1417b0a4c3bd7b17`:

```sh
./test.sh tests/unit/test_solution_backup_archive.py tests/unit/test_solution_file_payload_compression.py tests/unit/test_solution_zip_install.py tests/unit/test_solution_zip_install_cache.py tests/unit/routers/test_workspace_bundle_upload.py tests/unit/test_workspace_bundle_hardening.py tests/unit/test_solution_file_capture.py tests/unit/core/test_request_body_limit.py tests/unit/test_workspace_bundle_import.py tests/e2e/platform/test_solution_zip_install_e2e.py::test_export_round_trips_the_installed_bundle -v --durations=0
./test.sh quality api
```

The combined scoped suite passed all 66 cases in 43.50 seconds. It includes a real 268,313,994-byte synthetic file preview, rejection of corrupted payloads before writes for both install entry points, an encrypted disk-backed restore against real DB/object storage preserving source IDs, parent links and attachment bytes, unchanged source upload limits, config cache behavior, workspace import guards, and the existing HTTP install/export/reinstall journey. That retained HTTP journey spends 11.01 seconds in setup and 7.77 seconds in its call; its initial install and reinstall are the existing two jobs. The extended direct-service encrypted graph restore takes 1.03 seconds and adds no queued job.

API quality passed with zero pyright errors/warnings and all Ruff checks passing.

Meaningful red tests were captured before production edits for large archive/member support, archive payload streaming, bounded decryption, KDF allocation limits, upload budgets and pre-write payload corruption rejection. Private logs remain in `/tmp/docs-delivery-20261001/large-restore-*.log`.

This does not establish a full production backup restore. It removes extracted encrypted payload copies; multipart upload spooling, the staged archive download and browser Blob handling still need a separate storage/memory review and production-sized isolated restore proof. Complete backend/browser suites were not run locally; the repository merge gate owns broad candidate verification.

prs.title: Download durable Solution backups without browser Blob buffering
prs.body:
Durable Solution backups were downloaded through JavaScript as a Blob, retaining the entire archive in browser memory. Both the Solution export history and completion notification now request a short-lived, admin-authorized download link and let the browser download directly from object storage.

The link expires within ten minutes and never outlives the artifact. Unavailable or expired exports are rejected before signing, link responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`, and the existing authenticated streaming download endpoint remains available to CLI consumers. The API contract and generated client types are updated together.

The live download regression exposed legacy S3 signatures rejecting the requested ZIP content type and attachment disposition. Configure the shared S3 client with [Signature Version 4](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/boto3/latest/guide/s3-presigned-urls.html); existing signed GET and PUT consumers are verified alongside the new header overrides. Multipart upload IDs are validated before any parts are sent.

Validation, using the isolated Docker test stack:

- Meaningful red tests captured the Blob-buffering path, missing download-link handler, real S3 header-override HTTP 403, and invalid multipart upload IDs before their corresponding fixes.

- `./test.sh client e2e e2e/solution-backup-export.admin.spec.ts --project=platform-admin`: 2 passed, including native browser download of a real encrypted backup and exact byte comparison with the existing endpoint. No additional queued-job stage or test retry was added.

Regenerated the inventory with the existing Docker-based generator and recorded the added route; `./test.sh tests/unit/services/test_operation_inventory.py -v` now passes all 4 accounting/freshness checks. Commit `75399fcfb7451338381a976bb60f6efb296dd987` contains that repair and records the inventory repair. No CI retry was used to waive the failure.

Added the new endpoint with the same `CurrentSuperuser`/`solutions.read` classification as the existing streaming download and regenerated both projections using their existing Docker-based generators. `./test.sh tests/unit/test_access_list.py tests/unit/test_skill_appendix_fresh.py tests/unit/services/test_operation_inventory.py tests/unit/routers/test_solution_export_download_link.py -v`: 38 passed; final `./test.sh quality api`: Pyright 0 errors/0 warnings and Ruff passed. Full local backend, client-unit, and browser suites were not run; the merge queue remains the complete-suite gate.

This removes browser Blob buffering for durable backup downloads. It does not change the legacy synchronous export API, eliminate worker-local ZIP staging during export/restore, or establish production-size backup and restore capacity. That full delivery verification remains outstanding.

prs.title: Sweep agent runs stuck in cancelling
prs.body:
## Problem
Cancelling an agent run sets it to `cancelling` and relies on the worker to finish it. If the worker is gone, nothing ever completes the run: the stuck-run sweeper only handled `queued` and `running` agent runs. Production has agent runs that have sat in `cancelling` for over a month.

## Change
- The sweeper that already handles stuck workflow executions (every 5 minutes) now also marks agent runs `cancelled` once they have been in `cancelling` for 3 minutes (`CANCELLING_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`, the same rule as workflow executions). Chat runs get the same `cancelled` chat event the worker sends.
- The time is measured from when cancellation was requested, not from when the run started. Otherwise a long run cancelled seconds ago could be swept while its worker is still winding down; the worker's final write (partial output, tokens, duration) would then be skipped. New column `agent_runs.cancel_requested_at`, set by both cancel paths (`POST /api/agent-runs/{id}/cancel` and chat cancel).
- Migration `20261004_agent_run_cancel_req_at` adds the column and backfills runs already in `cancelling` with `coalesce(started_at, created_at)`, so they are swept on the first pass after deploy.

## Verification
- `./test.sh tests/unit/jobs/schedulers/test_execution_cleanup.py tests/unit/test_agent_run_cancel_requested_at.py tests/unit/test_timeout_zero_not_defaulted.py tests/unit/test_alembic_single_head.py -v`: 14 passed
  - covers: stale cancelling → cancelled; fresh cancelling untouched; started 60 min ago but cancelled 1 min ago is not swept; chat run gets a `cancelled` event; both cancel paths set the timestamp; backfill touches only cancelling rows
- `./test.sh quality api`: pyright 0 errors, ruff clean
- Full `./test.sh e2e`: 2136 passed
- Not run locally: full unit suite, client suites (no client changes)

prs.title: Audit retention: archive to object storage, verify, then clear
prs.body:
## What this does
Audit events no longer grow Postgres without limit. Admins set two windows in **Settings → Maintenance → Audit Retention**:
- **Keep in database:** events older than this move to an archive in object storage. The default is 90 days.
- **Keep in archive:** archived events older than this are deleted. The default is 365 days, and "Keep archives forever" is available.

Both ages are measured from when the event happened. One rule applies to every audit event, `access.check` included.

**Archive first, verify, then clear.** A row leaves Postgres only after it has been written to storage, read back, and verified (checksum, count, exact ids in order). The delete happens in the same short transaction that records the archived file in a catalog, and that transaction holds the job's current lease.

## Defaults
- **Existing installs:** the migration finds audit events already present and sets 90 days in the database and an unlimited archive. Nothing is ever deleted from the archive unless an admin changes that.
- **New installs:** 90 days in the database, 365 days in the archive.

## How it works
- **Daily job.** `audit.archive` is a PlatformJob that runs at 02:30 UTC (Run now and Preview are also available). It works through batches oldest first (at most 5,000 rows or about 64 MB per batch). Each batch is grouped per organization (or Global) and UTC day. Each group is written as deterministic JSONL.gz to `_audit/v1/org=<uuid|global>/day=<YYYY-MM-DD>/<sha256>.jsonl.gz`, read back and verified, and only then deleted. Each archived line includes a snapshot of the actor and organization names at archive time.
- **Restart safety.** The job freezes its windows in a checkpoint, so a retry continues with the same windows. The same rows always produce the same file name, so a rerun after a crash is safe.
- **Expiry.** Archived files are deleted page by page, inside a transaction that holds the lease.
- **Catalog.** `audit_archive_segments` records one row per archived file (no foreign keys, so archives outlive organizations).
- **New index.** `ix_audit_logs_created_id (created_at, id)`, built `CONCURRENTLY`.
- **Export (recovery).** `POST /api/audit/exports` runs an `audit.query` PlatformJob that combines archived and current events into one JSONL.gz file. It is downloaded from `GET /api/audit/exports/{job_id}/download`. The access rules are the same as the audit page:
  - Platform Admins can export everything.
  - Holders of `roleassignments.read` can export only `access.check*` events in the organizations they reach.
  - Access is checked when the export is requested, inside the job, and again at download.
  - Downloads expire after 7 days.
  - Archive and export share one lock and never run at the same time.
- **Audit page.** `GET /api/audit` now states its window to Platform Admins: "Showing events since …; older events are archived through …", with an Export button.
- **Preview.** Preview, and the confirmation shown when shortening the archive window, report exactly what would be archived and deleted. That includes events already past the archive window, which are archived and removed in the same run.
- **Runbook.** `docs/runbooks/audit-retention.md`.

## Deviations from the design, stated
- Export cleanup runs inside the daily archive job rather than as a separate hourly schedule.
- The Playwright happy path covers the card and Preview. Settings changes, the shortening confirmation and export are covered by vitest and backend e2e.
- `OrgReach` moved from `authorization/enforce.py` to `authorization/reach.py` so the scheduler doesn't import FastAPI (import hygiene). The class is unchanged.
- Leftover files: if an upload succeeds but its commit fails, and the rows change before the next run, the uploaded file stays in storage with no catalog row. It is ignored and never swept, because deleting after a failed commit is unsafe (the commit may have succeeded with the reply lost). This is documented in the runbook.

## Verification
- Full `./test.sh e2e`: 2158 passed, 0 failed (24.5 min)
- Focused backend tests: archiver (real Postgres + SeaweedFS: crash, corruption, stale lease, delete mismatch, expiry, storage unavailable), job handler unit tests, retention API, export (tenant isolation across archived and current rows, lost access, missing file), audit list, deny probe, decision matrix, access list, contract/DTO tripwires, org-scoping enforcement, alembic single head.
- `./test.sh quality api`: clean. `npm run tsc` clean, `npm run lint` 0 errors.
- vitest: service, settings card, banner, export dialog, AuditLogPage, Maintenance, Settings.
- Playwright: `e2e/audit-retention.admin.spec.ts`.
- Live drive on a port-mode debug stack: seeded old events, Preview, Run now (rows archived and catalogued), the shorten dialog showing the exact count, Cancel restoring the field, the banner, and an export downloaded with snapshot names. Screenshots in light, dark, desktop and phone width were sent for UX review.
- Not run locally: full vitest, full Playwright, `./test.sh pre-pr` (the merge queue runs them).

prs.body:
Solution apps could not discover their owning Solution, so Docs could not link to its native backup history. The host now forwards the already-loaded owning Solution ID through live and preview mounts, the SDK context, and new app scaffolds. prs.title: Run and event retention: delete finished runs after a window, keep cost history
prs.body:
## What this does
Finished runs and events no longer pile up in Postgres forever. Admins set one window in **Settings → Maintenance → Run history**: **30 days** by default, from 30 to 3650 days, or "Keep forever". It applies to new and existing installs alike. A daily job deletes:
- finished workflow runs: Success, Failed, Timeout, Cancelled, CompletedWithErrors and Stuck, counted from `completed_at`. Their logs go with them.
- finished agent runs and their steps: completed, failed, budget_exceeded, timeout and cancelled. Verdict history and flag conversations go with them.
- events (and their deliveries) older than the window. This replaces the hard-coded 30-day purge in `event_cleanup`, which is removed. Stuck-delivery cleanup stays.

These are never deleted: Scheduled, Pending, Running, Cancelling or paused runs, and any agent run that still has a child run. There is no archive; audit is the durable record.

## Cost and resource history is kept
**The rule:** every finished workflow run is counted exactly once. While it is kept, it is counted in `executions`. After it is deleted, it is counted in the new `workflow_run_daily` table. The daily row covers the run's day, org, workflow, name and status: run count, duration, CPU, peak cores/RSS/memory, AI cost and AI calls.
- **Same transaction.** The job writes the rollup in the same transaction that deletes the run. A crash therefore cannot lose a run or count it twice.
- **No hot path, no backfill.** Nothing writes the table outside the job, and no backfill is needed. With "Keep forever" the table stays empty.
- **AI usage rows outlive their runs.** The `ai_usage` foreign keys to `executions` and `agent_runs` are dropped. The ids stay as plain values, like `audit_logs.execution_id`. Just before a run is deleted, the job stamps `ai_usage.workflow_id` and `ai_usage.agent_id`. A side effect: deleting an agent no longer deletes its AI cost rows.
- **Reports read one source,** `workflow_run_source` (kept runs plus the rollup):
  - usage report summary and per-workflow CPU/memory;
  - by-workflow and by-agent AI cost;
  - the workflow resource report's **workflows view**, whose window now goes up to 366 days. The runs view still lists only kept runs, with a 31-day window.
  - all-time execution totals;
  - `/api/metrics/workflows`.
- **Tests:** e2e tests assert identical totals before and after deletion.
- **Dead columns dropped:** `execution_metrics_daily.total_ai_*` was never written.

## How it works
- **Daily job.** `run.retention` is a PlatformJob that runs at 03:00 UTC; Preview (dry run) and Run now are also available.
  - It deletes oldest first, in short batches: 1,000 workflow runs, 500 agent runs, 1,000 events.
  - Each batch holds the job's lease row lock, so a stale runner deletes nothing.
  - Each batch deletes exactly the selected ids. A count mismatch rolls the batch back.
  - It removes at most 100,000 rows per table per run, so a large first backlog is spread over several nights (shown as "continues tomorrow").
  - The cutoff is frozen in the checkpoint, so a retry deletes what the first attempt would have.
- **Agent runs are deleted leaves first.** The `parent_run_id` cascade therefore never removes a child.
- **Removed runs say so.**
  - **API:** 404 detail text for executions and agent runs (REST and the MCP gateway) now ends with "Finished runs are removed after N days." The status codes are unchanged.
  - **Client:** `useExecution` no longer polls a missing run every 2 s forever.
    - The run page and agent run page show "This run isn't available. Finished runs are removed after N days (retention)…" instead of an error with Retry.
    - Chat tool cards fall back to the recorded tool result.
    - Agent timeline rows show "Removed after N days (retention)".
  - **Public endpoint:** `GET /api/run-retention` returns `{days}` for this wording.
- **Migration** `20261006_run_retention`:
  - adds `workflow_run_daily`;
  - drops the two `ai_usage` FKs, with `lock_timeout` 5 s because the drop takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on `executions` / `agent_runs`;
  - adds the stamp columns;
  - drops the dead columns;
  - builds `(completed_at, id)` indexes on `executions` and `agent_runs` `CONCURRENTLY`, without `IF NOT EXISTS`.
- **Runbook:** `docs/runbooks/run-retention.md`. It covers half-migrated recovery and states that downgrade drops `ai_usage` rows of deleted runs.

## Production rollout
- No setting row exists, so prod gets 30 days. About 392k finished workflow runs and 12.9k agent runs are past 30 days; the backlog clears over about 4 nights.
- `executions` is 4 GB. Autovacuum makes the freed space reusable but does not shrink the files. Reclaiming the space is a separate, manual `pg_repack` decision.

## Deviations from the design, stated
- **FKs dropped, not set to NULL.** The `ai_usage` → run FKs are dropped instead of switched to `ON DELETE SET NULL`. That keeps run counts and source filters working unchanged, and the context check constraint keeps working too.
- **Rollup written at deletion, not at completion.** More than 20 code paths finish a run; deletion is one exact place.
- **Dropped inline runs merge.** In the usage report's by-workflow list, inline runs that are kept keep their own named rows. Deleted inline runs merge into "Inline or deleted workflow".
- **Small metrics change.** `/api/metrics/workflows` (no client caller) now windows on `started_at` (or `completed_at` for runs that never started), not `created_at`. Its averages count only runs that have the value.

## Verification
- Full `./test.sh unit`: 8293 passed, 0 failed. Full `./test.sh e2e`: 2183 passed, 0 failed (24.6 min). Both ran on the final head.
- Focused backend tests:
  - deleter against real Postgres: rollup, stamping, leaf-first agent deletion, stale lease, mismatch;
  - history-source before/after equality: usage report, resource report with status filter, inline runs, never-started runs, UTC day boundary;
  - job handler unit tests;
  - retention API: settings, preview, real run, `info` / `last_run`, 404 text, authorization;
  - migration catalog checks;
  - generators: access list, operation inventory, openapi digest;
  - deny probe;
  - contract/DTO tripwires.
- `./test.sh quality api` is clean. `npm run tsc` is clean and `npm run lint` has 0 errors. Full vitest: 544 files, 3455 tests passed.
- Playwright: `e2e/run-retention.admin.spec.ts`, plus `e2e/audit-retention.admin.spec.ts`, now scoped to its own card.
- Live drive on a port-mode debug stack with synthetic data (12,345 old runs, 210 agent runs, 4,000 events):
  - the shorten dialog showed exact counts;
  - Preview worked;
  - Run now deleted 12,345 / 210 / 4,000 and rolled up 12,345 runs;
  - the removed-run page rendered correctly.
  - Screenshots in light and dark, at desktop and phone width, were sent for UX review.

**UX approval is needed before merge.**

Sourced from pydantic-ai-slim's releases.

v2.53.0 (2026-10-01)

🛡️ Security

This release fixes one security issue in ConcurrencyLimitedModel. See the advisory for full details and affected versions.

  • GHSA-6fqq-452j-qhrp (high): a streamed request through ConcurrencyLimitedModel or limit_model_concurrency could keep its concurrency slot when the slot was released on a different task than the one that acquired it: after an early exit (the consumer stopped iterating, raised, or was cancelled), and also after fully consuming stream_text() with its default debouncing. Repeated streams could then block every request sharing the limiter. Agent-level max_concurrency and non-streaming requests are not affected. Reported by @​lche511. (#9478)

The fix also changes how limiters are shared: a model wrapper now raises UserError when it shares a limiter with the agent making the request or with an enclosing model wrapper, ConcurrencyLimiter.acquire() takes a slot on every call, even on the same task, and a custom AbstractConcurrencyLimiter must allow release() from another task.

Patched in 2.53.0. v1 is not affected.

prs.title: Explain access decisions: then vs now, what-if checks, and CLI
Person access page, Roles list and permission catalog (Effective Access)
prs.body:
## What this does
Admins can now see what a person can do, and where, on one page. Roles show what they grant, who holds them and where they apply. Nothing about enforcement changes.

- **Person page** (`/users/:userId`, tabs Access | Profile). It replaces the dialog that opened over the Users list.
  - **Header:** name, email, home organization and reach chips, plus a protected-account line when one applies. The ⋮ menu carries the same account actions as the list row: invites, Reset MFA, Sign Out of All Devices, Deactivate/Activate and Delete. Both places share one hook.
  - **Effective Access:** one row per place the person's roles reach (home, each placed org, All Customer Organizations, Global), with a column per permission area. Chips show the source role and place on hover or focus. A Platform Admin is one "All Permissions" chip.
  - **Role Assignments:** the editor now uses placement presets: Selected Organizations, All Customer Organizations, or All Organizations (= managed + provider org + Global). The presets offered are limited by the role and the caller.
    - A placement that matches no preset shows as Custom and is saved unchanged.
    - A role with a platform-wide permission placed on selected orgs gets a tappable warning.
  - **Quick edits:** the list row menu's Edit Profile still opens the dialog without leaving the list.
- **Roles list:** Built-in and Custom sections. Columns: grants (purple chips), holders, and where the role is placed (cyan chips).
- **Permission panel:** driven by the server's catalog, grouped by area and searchable. "Takes Effect with R3b" appears once per area that isn't enforced yet.
- **New routes:**
  - `GET /api/permissions/catalog`: every permission domain with Title Case name, area, actions, privileged permissions, scope (per organization / platform-wide / varies, derived from the access list), whether it's enforced, and display names. Readable by any signed-in user, because it's vocabulary only.
  - `GET /api/users/{id}/access`: the Effective Access map, gated exactly like the role-assignments read.
- **`RolePublic` gains** `holders`, `grants` and `placements`, computed only when consumer counts are (Platform Admins).
- **CLI:**
  - `bifrost permissions list`;
  - `bifrost users access <user>` (`users access check …` still works);
  - `bifrost users roles get <user>`;
  - `bifrost users roles set <user> [--base] [--role ROLE[=org:<ref>,customers,global,all]]… [--no-roles]`. `--base` alone keeps the current additional roles.
- **Shared pieces for PR 5:**
  - `--bf-reach*` and `--bf-power*` tokens, light and dark, with chip text at 5.47:1 or better;
  - a Badge `power` variant, plus `ReachChip`, `PermissionChip` and `GrantChip`;
  - a shared `EmptyState`;
  - the Badge warning variant moved to tokens.

## Copy rule (from review)
Display names follow Graph style in Title Case: Read / Read All / Read and Write, or the action's own verb (Run Workflows, Deploy Solutions). Everything that isn't a sentence is Title Case: buttons, headings, tabs, labels, badges, menu items. Sentences stay sentence case. The rule is written into `DESIGN.md`, with a one-line pointer in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

## Deviations, stated
- **`grants`, not `permissions`.** The new `RolePublic` field is named `grants`. R2b removed a free-form `permissions` dict from `RolePublic`, and older CLIs know that name with a different type.
- **Catalog gate.** The catalog is readable by any signed-in user rather than `roles.read`. Platform Operators can read access maps but not `roles.read@global`, and the map needs the catalog's areas.
- **Consumers column dropped** from the Roles list, to match the spec's columns. The counts are still on each role's tabs.
- **Test access lands in PR 5**, per spec §8.

## Verification
- On `3e6b085`: full `./test.sh unit` 8449 passed / 0 failed; full `./test.sh e2e` 2215 / 0. The Playwright specs for the changed journeys passed 15/15 (users, role-assignments, new user-access, roles detail, role lifecycle).
- After that, two client-only commits for chip styling and truncation: `./test.sh client unit` 561 files / 3595 tests passed, and the same Playwright specs 15/15 again, on the final head.
- `./test.sh quality api` is clean; `npm run tsc` is clean; `npm run lint` has 0 errors (5 existing warnings).
- Generated files: access list, operation inventory (REST 669, CLI 167), OpenAPI digest and CLI reference with plugin and codex mirrors, `v1.d.ts`, the decision matrix, `ENTITY_GROUPS` pin 19, export-count pins.
- The contract tripwire now covers the response shapes the CLI parses: the new ones, plus PR #914's explain, audit and retention shapes. The fingerprint was refreshed; it's additive, so `MIN_CLI_VERSION` is unchanged.
- **Reviews:**
  - each task reviewed and fixed; the copy, actions and chip tasks were reviewed by Codex;
  - a final whole-branch review with one fix wave;
  - screenshots reviewed by Jack (light and dark, 1440 and 390).
- **Live drive** on a port-mode debug stack with synthetic Contoso/Fabrikam data:
  - a Contoso person with a Helpdesk role at Fabrikam;
  - an Operator over all customer orgs;
  - a Platform Admin;
  - the Roles list and permission panel.

prs.title: Preserve completed evidence when agent delegation times out
prs.body:
When a specialist times out after completing diagnostic calls, its parent currently receives only a timeout error and can report those checks as never performed. Preserve a bounded receipt of captured tool results in the child run output and in the timeout error delivered to both autonomous and chat callers.

Receipts distinguish completed calls, failed calls, and unfinished operations, retain step/execution/child identifiers, and explicitly mark truncated or omitted evidence. Nested child receipts survive cancellation unwinding. The source is the executing child's own tool events and finalized descendants; tool arguments and its own model narrative are excluded. The durable error stays concise, and timeout/cancellation remain failure states. Existing delegation schemas, caller identity, organization boundaries, and successful output behavior are preserved.

The 600-second deadline remains. In the investigated read-only run, useful endpoint diagnostics were available at about 9m02s; a subsequent check was still running at the cutoff. Sequential checks, roughly 2m19s of orchestrator model time, and a rejected oversized-script preview explain the elapsed time. This evidence supports keeping the bounded deadline and preserving results, rather than increasing it. It does not establish an optimal deadline for every agent. Wall-clock wind-down policy is a separate follow-up.

Validation:
- `./test.sh tests/unit/services/test_autonomous_agent_executor.py tests/unit/services/test_agent_executor_tools.py -v`: 86 passed.
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/api/test_agent_delegation_lifecycle.py -v --durations=0`: 3 passed; new timeout persistence case took 0.13s excluding setup.
- Local replay of the captured incident: retained completed RMM, patch, and PowerShell facts and unfinished-call uncertainty; eight checks passed, 14,056 characters, zero external actions. Customer fixtures are not committed.
- `./test.sh pr-preflight`: passed repository consistency checks, API/client lint and types, 8,379 backend unit tests, 3,469 client tests, changed delegation E2E tests, and Python/JavaScript CodeQL (no findings on changed lines). Full preflight ran before updating to latest main; focused delegation tests and API quality checks were repeated after rebase.
- Full backend E2E and browser suites were not run locally; the merge queue remains the complete-suite gate.

Scope: in-process agent delegation shared by autonomous and chat callers. Independently queued MCP agent jobs and their root-run timeout are unchanged. Production deployment and representative live outcome verification remain pending.

Follow-up to #518.

prs.title: Re-evaluate Dependabot PRs after App follow-up commits
prs.body:
Dependabot automation must re-evaluate App-originated lockfile and canonical-disposition follow-ups. The sender restriction skips those events, so this gates on the authenticated Dependabot PR author while retaining pinned signed-commit metadata verification.

Adds a regression contract covering the workflow gate and verification boundary, and runs it in CI. Baseline failed against current main; Node 26 now passes all 9 automation tests. Workflow YAML parsing and diff checks passed. Application suites are delegated to the merge queue.


Postmerge deployment: run37582922775 timed out while one old worker completed its graceful drain. The declared 360-second drain allowance and serial six-worker rollout exceed the universal five-minute rollout watch; no retries or timeout/drain changes were applied. Independent Kubernetes verification afterward confirmed API2/client2/scheduler1/worker6 all Ready on image1.4.2-dev.1791354301, with no terminating or old-image Bifrost pods. Log evidence: /tmp/bifrost-security-deploy938.log.

prs.title: fix: preserve final agent handoff with Pydantic AI 2.54
prs.body:
Pydantic AI 2.54 defers recording a request until after the response hook. At a two-request limit, Bifrost therefore allowed a second tool action and returned `budget_exceeded` instead of a final handoff. Account for the current response’s request in wind-down so the last allowed response stops further tool calls. Token accounting and hard limits remain intact.

Includes the dependency update from #935 and its compatibility repair. The original Dependabot PR remains blocked and will be superseded by this tested pair.

Validation: reproduced the failure before the fix; 5 focused regression tests and 96 runtime/executor/profile-consumer tests passed in Docker; backend Ruff and Pyright passed. Full merge-queue checks remain required. Internal dependency compatibility maintenance is omitted from in-app notes.


Final delivery verification: complete merge-queue CI37585876268 passed and merged20c786a59bca374561fb8a5b2acd7f33fd6da1b6. Main CodeQL37587530690 passed. Deployment run37587530589 exceeded the existing five-minute worker rollout watch while the final old worker drained. Independent live verification afterward confirmed exactly API2/client2/scheduler1/worker6 Ready on image1.4.2-dev.1791357104, with no old-image or terminating Bifrost pods. Live API runs pydantic-ai-slim2.54.0 and its budget file SHA2569e25d07f74b48f089613d82795e831ce4a79eaa6eb67c07638fc15ed730e3ecf matches the tested source. No retries, longer timeouts, or shortened worker drains were used. Log evidence: /tmp/bifrost-security-deploy939.log. Original935 is closed as superseded.

prs.title: Managed identities: Identities tab, workflow access, Test Access, Access Checks
prs.body:
## What this does
Admins can see and manage the identities that unattended workflows run as. They can pick which identity a workflow runs as, grant it what its past runs needed, test what anyone could do, and review every recorded check that would be denied once enforcement is on. Nothing is enforced yet: every check stays report-only (`enforced: false`).

- **Users | Identities tabs** (`/users`, `/users/identities`).
  - Each organization's default identity, the Global default, and custom identities. The Global one is pinned first.
  - Columns: Organization (always first, per the new `DESIGN.md` → Tables rule), Name, Kind, Roles, Workflows Using.
  - New Identity (name + organization or Global); rename and delete custom identities. Deleting one that a workflow runs as is refused with the workflows named.
  - **Every default identity is called "Default Identity"** and its name can't be edited. Wherever one appears, its organization appears with it: org chip + hexagon glyph in the UI, `Default Identity (Contoso)` in the CLI and server messages.
  - **Identity names are unique per organization**, case-insensitive, with Global as one scope. Enforced by a database index; a clash is a 409 that names the organization.
  - The person page doubles as the identity page: hexagon glyph instead of an avatar, no email, profile is the name only, and the base role is fixed for defaults.
- **Workflow access panel** (workflow Edit → Access tab).
  - **Runs Unattended As**: the identities this workflow may use (`run_identity_allowed`). The change saves right away.
  - **Create a Dedicated Identity**: named "{Workflow} Identity" in the workflow's organization, then selected.
  - **Recommended Access**: "Based on this workflow's runs in the last N days, {identity} would also need:". Computed from the recorded `access.check` rows: organizations outside the identity's reach, policy roles it lacks, and workflow roles (shown as information).
    - **Grant to Identity** grants a policy role. **Grant Access** opens a role picker, limited to grantable roles, and places the role at the organization the identity can't reach yet.
    - Both read the identity's current roles, merge the grant and write them back. On a default identity they first ask to confirm, naming every workflow that shares it, and offer to create a dedicated identity instead.
  - **Reach Summary** (person-started vs unattended), read-only access mode (Full), and Test Access prefilled with the workflow and its identity.
  - **Delegation check**: making a workflow run as a non-default identity requires holding every power that identity holds. Platform Admins pass. Today only superusers edit workflows, so this is a no-op for current users.
- **Test Access**. Asks "could this person or identity do X in organization Y (optionally inside workflow Z)?" and answers with a step-by-step trace; stopped steps are amber, "Would Stop Here". Available on the person page and in the workflow panel. Operations are offered by name (Read Agents); any access-list key can still be typed.
- **Audit event drawer**.
  - Opened from any audit row (keyboard too).
  - Access checks show the stored trace. **Test Again Now** shows Then and Now side by side, with changed steps marked.
  - Older rows without a stored trace, archived events and unavailable inputs each explain themselves in one sentence.
- **Access Checks page** (`/audit/access-checks`, gated on holding `roleassignments.read` anywhere). The would-deny list:
  - grouped by Workflow, Resource Type or Organization;
  - drill-in to individual checks (shareable URL), then the drawer.
  - Operators see their reach; Platform Admins see everything.
- **API**:
  - `GET/POST /api/identities`, `PATCH/DELETE /api/identities/{id}`;
  - `GET /api/workflows/{id}/run-identities`;
  - `GET /api/workflows/{id}/recommended-access`;
  - `GET /api/audit` gains `workflow_id` / `organization_id` filters (UUID or `none`).
  - Audit entries now carry `workflow_name` and the acting user's own `home_organization_*` (not the target organization).
  - `WorkflowPublic.permission_mode`, `UserPublic.identity_kind`, `RoleUser.identity_kind`.
- **CLI**:
  - `bifrost users list --identities`;
  - `bifrost users create --identity --org <org|global> --name`;
  - `bifrost workflows update <wf> --run-as <identity> | --run-as-default`;
  - `bifrost workflows recommendations <wf>`;
  - `bifrost workflows grant <wf> (--recommendation N | --all) [--yes]` (`--yes` required on a default identity);
  - identities resolve by name or by their label (`"Default Identity (Contoso)"`) anywhere a user is accepted;
  - `audit list --group-by workflow|organization` prints names, not IDs.
- **Migration `20261007_custom_global_identity`**:
  - renames every default identity to "Default Identity" (about 95 rows in prod);
  - lets custom identities be Global;
  - adds the per-organization unique name index;
  - adds `ix_audit_logs_access_check_workflow` (concurrently) so Recommended Access doesn't scan the hot audit window.
  - The downgrade restores the old generated names. Rehearsal test included.
  - Any environment that ran an earlier cut of this branch and created two same-named custom identities in one organization must rename one before upgrading. Prod has no custom identities.

## Rulings I made (cost if wrong)
- R1: the delegation check on `PATCH run_identity_id` ships now. Cost: one guard.
- R4/R5: New Identity offers organizations from the identities list plus `/api/organizations` (when readable), filtered by `users.lifecycle.readwrite`. Cost: none.
- R7: reach items carry no automatic grant (any role placed at an organization gives reach; auto-picking would hand out powers), so the panel asks for a role. Cost: a UI flow.
- R8: the workflow-role item appears only when the workflow's organization is Global or the identity's home. Cost: one information item.
- R10a/R10b: recommendations carry `organization_id`; Runs Unattended As saves immediately, with an inline error and revert. Cost: one field / moving it into the footer Save.
- R11: `workflows grant` to a default identity requires `--yes`, matching the UI confirm. Cost: one flag.
- R12: removed `GET /api/users?identities=only` (no consumer left). Cost: re-adding a filter.
- R13/R15: server messages and audit entries name identities with their place and workflows by name, resolved server-side. Cost: two fields.
- R14: audit `workflow_id` / `organization_id` filters; explain on a row without a stored trace answers `then: null` instead of a 500. Cost: two filters.
- R16: partial expression index on `audit_logs` for access checks by workflow. Cost: one index on prod `audit_logs`.
- R17: a CLI user reference falls through to identities by name or label. Cost: one resolution path.
- R18/R19: role holders show identities as identities; trace outcome lines are Title Case status labels. Cost: one field / copy.
- Superseded by your final answers: R3 (no uniqueness) and R6 ("{Org} Identity" names).

## Known follow-ups (PR 6)
- The audit list's `action` filter is a prefix match, so the new partial index serves Recommended Access but not the Access Checks drill-in. Slim rows and Entra-style grouping in PR 6 touch the same query.
- The CLI resolves workflows by code name, not display name (existing behaviour).

## Verification
On `1f17d37a2` (branch merged with `origin/main` at `2e125fee8`; test stack rebuilt for main's dependency bumps):
- `./test.sh unit`: **8574 passed / 0 failed** (on `de92bd04f`; the two later commits are covered by the targeted runs below).
- `./test.sh e2e`: **2255 / 2256**. The one failure was this PR's own: `test_mcp_parity` flagged `run_identity_id`, which the CLI now hides behind `--run-as`. Fixed in `75f54a6c0` and declared as an MCP `extra_arg`, the same way `ConfigCreate.organization_id` is. `test_mcp_parity.py` + `test_dto_flags.py` + `test_cli_audit.py`: 145/145.
- `./test.sh client unit`: **583 files / 3771 tests passed**. `npm run tsc` clean; `npm run lint` 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings).
