prs.title: Hardening: credential-free package steps, secret-bound MCP sign-in codes, notification dismiss rule
prs.body:
Three small hardening changes. Nothing changes for anyone using these features as intended.

## What changes

1. **Build and install steps no longer inherit platform credentials.** The following run with an allowlisted environment (`shared/subprocess_env.package_tool_env`): `pip` in the requirements setup and package installs, and `npm` and `vite` in app builds. It keeps only `PATH`, `HOME`, locale, proxy and CA settings and the tool's own settings. Platform secrets, database, storage, queue and cache credentials are never passed to package code. A guard test fails on any new `pip`, `npm`, `npx` or `uv` subprocess under `api/src` or `api/shared` that doesn't pass an explicit `env=`.
2. **MCP sign-in codes are bound to the server secret.** The authorization code's storage key and its record are keyed with an HMAC of the server secret, and the record carries an HMAC tag that `/token` verifies with a constant-time compare. These all return `invalid_grant`, never a 500: an unknown or expired code, a reused code, a changed record, an invalid record, and a badly formed tag. Codes issued before deploy expire within their normal five-minute lifetime.
3. **Dismissing an admin notification follows the same rule as reading it.** A user can still dismiss their own notifications. Only callers who can see admin notifications can dismiss them.

## Testing

- `./test.sh unit`: 8633 passed, 0 failed.
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/platform/test_worker_requirements_setup.py tests/e2e/api/test_notifications.py`: 11 passed.
- New unit tests:
  - `tests/unit/test_package_tool_env.py`: the allowlist, every call site, and the AST guard;
  - `tests/unit/services/mcp_server/test_auth_code_binding.py`: round trip, guessed key, tampered record, reuse, invalid JSON, non-hex, lone-surrogate and wrong-length tags;
  - `tests/unit/services/test_notification_service.py`.
- Live check in the test stack: `pip install --dry-run` and `npm` both ran successfully with the scrubbed environment.
- `./test.sh quality api`: clean.
- `./test.sh pr-preflight`: everything passed except one client unit test, `access-operations.test.ts`. That failure is a harness defect from #942: the client-check runner's build context has no `docs/generated`. It's unrelated to this branch, and a dedicated fix follows in its own PR.
- Reviews: Codex task review plus two scoped re-reviews; clean.

## Rulings I made (each with its cost if wrong)

- **The CLI's local `npm` and `pip` subprocesses (`api/bifrost`) are out of scope.** The CLI runs on the developer's own machine with their own credentials. Cost if wrong: a developer's local tools see their own environment, as today.
- **A record signed with the real secret but missing fields can still error.** Only the server can sign records, so this isn't reachable. Cost if wrong: a 500 on a record the server itself wrote incorrectly.
- **Superusers can still read any notification by ID.** That's a pre-existing gap, tracked for its own fix. Cost if wrong: it stays open until that fix.

prs.title: fix(app-sdk): renew session on 401 for v1 table calls
prs.body:
## Product Updates

- [ ] Highlight
- [x] Other — Inline (v1) apps no longer lose table reads and saves when the 30-minute session cookie lapses; they renew the session and retry.
- [ ] Omit

Disposition: `product-updates/dispositions/pr-964.json` (`other`, `category: fix`), validated with `scripts/product_updates.py validate`.

## Summary

**Symptom.** In inline v1 apps, table reads and saves fail some time after the last session renewal with `tables: 401 {"detail":"Not authenticated"}`. Newly mounted `useTable` hooks resolve to `rows: []` with `error` set, so apps that don't render `error` show data as missing. Saves either toast the 401 or silently vanish. Reported by a customer on a v1 CRM app: account info "randomly unavailable" when opening another location, and edits disappearing several times a day.

**Root cause.** The `access_token` and `csrf_token` cookies have `Max-Age=1800`. v1 apps never mount `<BifrostProvider>`, so the data SDK's `http()` (`client/src/lib/app-sdk/tables.ts`) does a bare same-origin cookie `fetch` with no 401 handling, and nothing in a v1 app renews the cookie. It only recovers when some other host code path happens to call `refreshAccessToken()`. v2 apps are unaffected: `BifrostProvider.authedFetch` already refreshes once via the host bridge and retries.

**Fix.**
- `http()` now renews through the host bridge (`__BIFROST_PLATFORM_AUTH_V1__.refreshAccessToken`, the same single-flight refresh `authedFetch` uses) and retries **once** on a 401. It re-reads the rotated CSRF token for the retry.
  - This applies only to the same-origin (v1) transport; the provider transport keeps owning renewal.
  - It honors `canRefreshAccessToken()`, so embed sessions are unchanged.
  - An unrecoverable 401 (refresh fails, or retry still 401) calls `handleAuthenticationFailure()`, as `authedFetch` does, and still throws the same error.
- The bridge type and accessor move from `provider.tsx` to `transport.ts` (`getPlatformAuth()`), so `tables.ts` and `provider.tsx` share one definition.

**Validation.**
- Unit:
  - New `tables.test.ts` cases: retry succeeds; rotated CSRF on the retried mutation; retry result still gets 404→null handling; renewal fails; still-401 retries at most once; embed session; no bridge; provider transport untouched; parallel burst.
  - New `transport.test.ts`.
  - New `use-table.test.tsx` case: the snapshot recovers. This case fails against `main`'s `tables.ts` with `error: tables: 401 …`.
- Commands (on the rebased branch):
  - `npx vitest run src/lib/app-sdk/` → 21 files / 249 tests pass.
  - `npm run tsc` → pass.
  - `npm run lint` → 0 errors. The 5 warnings are pre-existing, in untouched files.
  - Before the rebase, the full client unit suite (`npm test`) passed: 568 files / 3632 tests.
- Live before/after on a local `./debug.sh` stack (port mode). The repro is an inline_v1 app that mirrors the reporting app's table access: an explicit org `scope` on every call, a card that mounts its own `useTable` when opened, a field `update`, and an `insert`. Chromium runs in `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-jammy`, which signs in, clears the `access_token` cookie to simulate the 30-minute lapse, then opens a card and saves.
  - **Before** (`main`): the new card shows `Unknown provider` with `tables: 401 {"detail":"Not authenticated"}`. PATCH 401, POST 401, and no `/api/auth/refresh` call.
  - **After**: 2× query 401 → **one** `200 /api/auth/refresh` → 2× query 200. The card renders the row, PATCH returns 200 and insert 201.
  - With `refresh_token` also cleared: before, the page stays put showing the 401; after, it redirects to `/login?returnTo=…`.
- Not run: backend suites (no backend change), client e2e suite.


**Delayed-response recovery.** Table calls now compare the host token captured before sending with the current token after a 401. If another request already renewed the session, they retry once without renewing again. A deterministic regression test releases eleven original 401 responses one at a time after the first renewal completes and verifies that all calls recover with one renewal and no authentication-failure handoff. The existing burst test now clears its single-flight lock after completion, matching the real host.

**Out of scope / follow-ups.**
- `files.ts` uses the same cookie-only pattern without renewal.
- The v1 table websocket treats close code 4001 as non-retryable (`ws-client.ts`), so live updates can stop after expiry until remount.

prs.title: Name every elevated permission and record it report-only
prs.body:
Every place where being a superuser, a Platform Admin, a provider-organization member or a scope-bypass caller grants something now has a **named permission**. Each one is recorded **report-only** in Access Checks (`access.check`, `enforced: false`). Nothing is refused or enforced, nothing returns differently, and nobody's access changes. Enforcement comes area by area at cutover. After that, the flag checks are deleted and Platform Admin becomes a role that holds every permission.

## What changes

**Permission names follow Microsoft Graph**

- The format is `resource.action[.all]`, lowercase, with one word per resource.
- Actions:
  - `read` and `readwrite`;
  - `readbasic`, the everyday view: only what's shared with you, without management detail;
  - a resource's own verb: Run Workflows, Run Agents, Use AI, Impersonate Users, Publish Apps, Deploy Solutions, Build Solutions.
- `.all` means other people's private items. It is allowed only on agents, agent runs, artifacts, workflow runs, Home collections and platform jobs, and it never widens reach.
- Display names follow the rule exactly: Read X, Read Basic X, Read and Write X, Read All X, Read and Write All X.
- New resources: AI Model Information (`ai`), Artifacts, Home Collections, Platform Jobs, Privileged Access, Table Row Attribution.
- Renamed (data migration; no custom role holds them in production):
  - `apps.deploy.execute` → `apps.publish`
  - `solutions.deploy.execute` → `solutions.deploy`
  - `solutions.build.execute` → `solutions.build`
  - `users.lifecycle.readwrite` → `userlifecycle.readwrite`
- The old `.read.all` strings (detail views) move to the Graph meaning:
  - full-view reads become `x.read`;
  - the User and Operator roles' everyday reads become `x.readbasic`.

**Built-in roles** (migration, with downgrade and rehearsal)

- **User:** the read-basic views, plus Run Workflows, Run Agents, Use AI and Read AI Model Information. These keep today's launches working once launches are enforced.
- **Platform Operator:** gains Run Agents.
- Platform Admin and Secrets Reader are unchanged.

**Every route names its permission**

- 88 routes that had no permission now name one. Each is either the permission the route requires, or the permission its admin-only branch uses, since your own items need nothing.

**Every elevated check in the code is registered with its replacement**

- `api/tests/unit/test_access_list.py` registers 286 code locations.
- Each one maps to a permission, `reach`, `route`, `system`, `cutover` or `delete`, and is pinned by the number of elevated checks in that function. A new elevated branch fails the test.
- The scan reaches beyond REST, WebSocket and MCP routes:
  - the MCP mount and its middleware, dynamically registered MCP tools, PlatformJob handlers, queue consumers, scheduler jobs, startup, and the SDK package;
  - string-keyed flag reads and computed elevation;
  - token minting, Redis-held identity data, and package-install subprocesses.
- An invariant test fails if any replacement permission is held by the User or Operator role. Enforcement can therefore never hand an ordinary user an admin power.

**Report-only recording**

- **People's own requests are now recorded too.**
  - At every registered power site, and at every launch or open, the code notes the named permission with the object's organization. Global objects launch in the caller's organization.
  - The note is judged in the background against the person's own roles, or for a run against the run user plus the workflow's added powers.
  - Only would-deny results are written. Decisions are deduplicated once per day before judging, using Redis reservations with ownership tokens.
- Access Checks and the audit drawer show the permission's display name. The CLI's `audit` output names it too.

**Surfaces**

- The permission catalog lists every assignable permission.
- `operations.md` marks the permissions that apply only to other people's items.
- `DESIGN.md` gains the naming rule.
- The Platform Operator description now says Operators run agents.
- `v1.d.ts` is regenerated.

## For review

- **Visible UI change:** the role permission panel now lists every held permission. It no longer folds `read` into `readwrite`, which matches the rule "no implicit hierarchy".
- **Audit-week noise to expect:** provider-organization members who aren't admins will record would-denies when they open shared agents outside their reach, because the elevated branch fires even where sharing would also admit them.

## Testing

- `./test.sh unit`: 8848 passed.
- `./test.sh e2e` (full backend): 2273 passed, on the Task 6 head. A later fix pass touched only the test registry, the migration mapping, note placement on user routes, and one `except`. The rehearsal and unit suite were re-run after it.
- `./test.sh client unit`: 3810 passed.
- `npm run tsc` and lint: clean.
- `./test.sh quality api`: clean.
- Migration rehearsals: 14 passed. They check the built-in roles end exactly at their frozen sets, and that downgrade restores the previous state.

- Reviews: Codex review for each task, with fix rounds until clean; then a whole-branch review (verdict: ready to merge, with its findings fixed in one pass).

## Rulings I made (each with its cost if wrong)

1. **Global workflows, apps, forms and agents launch in the caller's organization.** Run Workflows means "may launch at all, in this org", and Global defaults are read at home. Cost if wrong: one function (`launch_target`) changes.
2. **Bypassing an object's access setting is recorded as `reach`, not as a launch permission.** This is consistent with REST workflow execute. Cost if wrong: cutover still has to decide who may launch items not shared with them.
3. **No implicit permission hierarchy:** `readwrite` doesn't imply `read`, and `read` doesn't imply `readbasic`. Cost if wrong: a custom role holding only `apps.read` couldn't open apps at enforcement. Production has no custom roles, and the migration maps custom `x.read` to `x.readbasic`.
4. **`workflows.read.all` maps to `roles.read` only**, not to all of Read Settings. Cost if wrong: a custom role (none in production) loses the workflow-keys view.
5. **Solution permission requests keep their stored strings,** because renaming them would invalidate approved digests. Production has 0 rows. Cost if wrong: an install with a pending request re-requests it.
6. **Merged `.all` reads aren't restored on downgrade.** This is documented and no built-in role holds them. Cost if wrong: a downgraded custom role loses the old string.
7. **Internal jobs that act with system access on an object a route already authorized are `system`.** They move to a service principal at cutover. Cost if wrong: the value gets renamed later.
8. **The Platform Admin role ID and the wildcard aren't treated as elevated tokens,** because they are the post-cutover mechanism. The role-name check is. Cost if wrong: role-ID checks need their own review at cutover.
9. **Scanner false positives are acceptable; false negatives are not.** Over-matching forces a registration; under-matching would hide a check. Cost if wrong: an occasional registration a reviewer has to justify.
10. **Judging is deduplicated per person or run, kind, operation, permission, target and subject, once a day, before any database work.** Cost if wrong: a role change shows in Access Checks the next day.
11. **People record `scope_switch` would-denies as well as permission would-denies.** That way the audit week sees who relies on cross-organization reach. Cost if wrong: more background judging on provider-staff list requests.
12. **The power-site binding test checks presence per function,** and branch precision is covered by per-site unit tests. Cost if wrong: a note on the wrong branch is caught only by unit tests or review.
13. **Repeated identical notes on user writes collapse through the reservation key.** Cost if wrong: a few extra Redis `SET NX` calls.
14. **Product Updates: highlight,** "Named Permissions in Access Checks", report-only wording. Cost if wrong: the copy changes.

prs.title: Run agents as another user; one Impersonate Users permission for Run As
prs.body:
Closes #943

Agents can now **run as another user**, and one permission, **Impersonate Users** (`users.impersonate`, privileged), governs both workflow and agent `run_as`. Before this, workflow `run_as` was allowed only for superusers, and agents had no `run_as` at all.

## What changes

**One rule for Run As**

- The caller needs Impersonate Users in the target user's organization. A privileged target also needs Read and Write Privileged Access.
- **Who can now do it:**
  - Platform Admins keep it through their wildcard.
  - An explicit role grant now works too.
  - Everyone else still gets 403.
- **Refusals:**
  - The 403 comes before any user lookup, and every refusal uses the same message.
  - Inactive users, the system account and managed identities can't be Run As targets (400). Production had 8 `run_as` calls in the last 30 days, and none targeted any of these.
  - An organization-scoped agent can't act as a user from another organization (400).
- Naming yourself is a plain launch. For workflows, naming the run user keeps today's `run_as=context.user_id` pattern working, including for runs that act as a managed identity.

**The three identities stay separate**

| | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Acting user | Whose identity the tools use |
| Initiator | Who asked |
| Run user | Whose reach the run has |

- `run_as` changes only the acting user. It never lifts reach.
- Agent runs record the acting user in the new column `agent_runs.run_as_user_id`, with a partial index. It is loaded from the database when the run starts, never from Redis.
- Every tool, workflow tool and delegated child acts as that user. An impersonated external user keeps their External restrictions in tools.
- Tool input can't choose the acting user. A test covers all 94 system tools, plus the workflow and delegation paths.

**Launch paths and re-checks**

- `POST /api/agent-runs/enqueue` and `/execute`, reruns, and the SDK's `agents.enqueue` / `agents.run(run_as=…)`.
- A rerun decides Run As again for whoever reruns it, using the target's current organization.
- A delayed or scheduled workflow `run_as` is decided again when it fires. An initiator who has since been deactivated, or who lost the grant, is refused, and the refusal is audited.

**Visibility and audit**

- Initiators can read the root runs they started as someone else, through every execution read.
- Every impersonation by a person is recorded as an enforced Access Check, success or failure, including refused attempts by someone who holds Impersonate Users nowhere.
- `run_as` from inside a workflow (an engine token) stays on the staged rule until cutover, and is recorded report-only.
- The agent run page shows Run As, falling back to the email when the name is empty. Access Check traces read in plain sentences.

**SDK and docs**

- The SDK's `AgentRunHandle.run_as_user_id` and `AgentRun.run_as_user_*` fields.
- `llms.txt` gains a Run As section. Docs-site pages follow in their own PR.

**Calls without `run_as` are unchanged:** the same rows, payloads, status codes and audit rows. Every touched launch path has a regression assertion for this.

## Testing

- `./test.sh unit`: 9067 passed.
- `./test.sh client unit`: 3820 passed. `npm run tsc` and lint: clean.
- `./test.sh quality api`: clean.
- `./test.sh e2e` (full backend): 2279 passed.
- `./test.sh pr-preflight`: passed (unit 9067, changed e2e files 19, client 3820, CodeQL Python and JavaScript on changed lines: 0 alerts).
- Live drive on the test stack:
  - an explicit Impersonate Users grant allows `run_as`, and Access Checks records an enforced success;
  - after the grant is revoked, the same call is refused, and `audit explain` shows "then passed, now stopped".
- Reviews: a Codex review for each of the 12 tasks, with fix rounds until clean. A whole-branch review then found 0 Critical, 0 Important and 7 Minor issues. The minors are listed below as follow-ups.

## Rulings I made (each with its cost if wrong)

1. **Workflow-originated `run_as` stays staged:** it is report-only now and enforced at cutover. Cost if wrong: one more area to flip at cutover.
2. **Managed identities are refused as Run As targets.** Assign the identity to the workflow or agent instead. Cost if wrong: a later small change allows them.
3. **An organization-scoped agent refuses a target from another organization.** Cost if wrong: a later change runs it in the agent's org.
4. **No CLI or MCP Run As flags in this PR.** Cost if wrong: a follow-up adds them (CLI flag `--as-user`).
5. **Every enforced impersonation is written to the audit log, not deduplicated per day.** Cost if wrong: more audit rows for a rare action.
6. **A refused attempt by someone holding Impersonate Users nowhere is audited at their own organization.** Cost if wrong: extra audit rows.
7. **Naming the run user acts as the run user, with an existence check only.** Cost if wrong: none, since today's identity is preserved.
8. **A service token naming its own run user stays 403.** Cost if wrong: such an integration keeps getting 403, as it does today.
9. **A person naming themselves on an agent launch is a no-op.** Cost if wrong: self-named runs show no Run As.
10. **A rerun re-applies the organization rule.** Cost if wrong: a rerun whose target moved organizations fails with 400.
11. **A delayed run re-checks the initiator's activity and grant, and audits refusals.** Cost if wrong: a deactivated user's queued run fails instead of running.
12. **Agent runs re-check only target activity at start.** They're authorized at launch and queued for seconds. Cost if wrong: a grant revoked in those seconds doesn't stop the run.
13. **One read rule for initiators across every execution read; cancel stays acting-user only.** Cost if wrong: an initiator can read logs and results through those endpoints too.
14. **`run_as_user_email` is added beside the name, and the acting user column gets a partial index.** Cost if wrong: one extra field and one small index.
15. **Product Updates: highlight,** "Run Agents as Another User". Cost if wrong: the copy changes.

## Review minors, fixed in this PR

- **Holders learn nothing about users outside their reach.** Someone holding Impersonate Users gets the same 403 for an unknown user and for any user their grant doesn't cover.
  - The caller's organization records only the request, in the same row shape for both cases.
  - The user's own organization records the full decision, unless that is the caller's organization.
- **Refused re-checks of delayed runs are recorded** for engine rows and person rows, including a target deleted after scheduling.
- **The initiator can cancel a scheduled root run they started as someone else.** This uses the same rule as reads, and children are not newly cancellable.
- **One `acting_target` helper,** shared e2e builders, and a promoter docstring.
- **Verification after the fixes:** unit 9078 passed; targeted e2e passed (`test_agent_run_as`, `test_workflow_mutations_service`, `test_workflow_scheduling_flow`, `test_execution_identity_matrix`, `test_executions`, `test_audit_access_checks`, `test_access_explain`); `quality api` clean; CodeQL Python and JavaScript on changed lines: 0 alerts.

## Remaining follow-ups (own PRs)

- The CLI `--as-user` flag.

**Cutover list:**

- runs without `run_as` still trust the Redis caller;
- the `is_platform_admin` / `is_superuser` key mismatch, and the missing External and provider flags on those runs' tool context;
- nested `run_as` through the MCP bridge token.

prs.title: Fix CLI device login throttling and expiry
prs.body:
## Product Updates

- [x] Other — CLI browser login keeps waiting through temporary throttling and stops when its device code expires.

## Summary

Device login advertised five-second polling but limited the token endpoint to ten requests per minute, causing the CLI to exit on its eleventh poll. Give token polling its documented twenty-request budget, recover from HTTP 429 and OAuth `slow_down`, respect `Retry-After`, and bound polling by the advertised expiry using a monotonic clock.

Other authentication endpoints retain their existing rate limits. No API schema or CLI contract changes.

Fixes #969

prs.body:
## Product Updates

- [ ] Highlight — list the entry UUID(s), or say that the entry is being drafted before this PR receives a number.
- [x] Other — Deleting an integration now stops its OAuth token refreshes and the repeated refresh-failed alerts.
- [ ] Omit — give the concrete reason this has no announcement value.

The canonical disposition is committed as `product-updates/dispositions/pr-<number>.json` with `review.status: draft` for maintainer approval.

## Summary

Fixes #973

Deleting an integration only soft-deleted it, leaving its OAuth provider and tokens in place. The `oauth_token_refresh` scheduler kept refreshing them and, once refresh failed, emitted `integration.refresh_failed` + `integration.reauth_required` every 15 minutes with no UI path left to disconnect them. - `api/src/routers/integrations.py`: `delete_integration` still soft-deletes the integration, and now also clears `integration_mappings.oauth_token_id` for the integration's tokens and deletes its `oauth_tokens` and `oauth_providers` rows.
- `api/src/jobs/schedulers/oauth_token_refresh.py`: the refresh query outer-joins `integrations` and skips providers whose integration is soft-deleted, so orphans created before this change stop alerting without a data migration. Providers with no integration (MCP servers, standalone connections) are unaffected.

prs.title: Isolate MCP OAuth ownership and clean retired integration credentials
prs.body:
## Product Updates

- [x] Other — MCP OAuth setup uses independent providers; historical credentials of deleted integrations are removed. Existing provider-ID API payloads require inline OAuth configuration; installations with shared MCP credentials must reconnect before upgrading.

MCP server create/update requests could attach an existing integration-owned OAuth provider by UUID. This removes that request field and rejects legacy payloads with 422; the normal inline OAuth setup continues creating an independent provider. Manifest import rejects integration-owned provider references while retaining independent provider IDs for round trips.

The migration removes providers and tokens belonging to soft-deleted integrations after clearing mapping token links. Live integration credentials, standalone providers, and independent MCP credentials are preserved. If an existing MCP server or MCP credential shares an integration-owned provider, migration stops before modifying data and identifies the affected UUIDs so the operator can configure independent MCP OAuth and reconnect. Deleted credentials cannot be restored by downgrade; there is no schema change to reverse.

Follow-up to #974 and #973. Paul’s PR remains unchanged and handles deletion going forward plus the scheduler filter for historical deleted integrations. This follow-up lands after #974. Combined focused verification was performed with #974 applied.

Updates `altcha` from 3.2.4 to 3.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from altcha's releases.

v3.3.0

This release fixes the widget's proof-of-work code to match the fixed altcha-lib (v2.6.0). It fixes a key-derivation mismatch that caused valid solutions to be rejected, and a verification bypass in altcha/lib. Upgrading is recommended.

Security

  • verifySolution bypass (altcha/lib). If the challenge had no keySignature, or the verifier passed no hmacKeySignatureSecret, verifySolution re-derived the key from the submitted counter but never checked it against the signed keyPrefix. Any counter, for example 0, together with its derived key verified without doing any work. The derived key must now also match keyPrefix. altcha-lib fixed this in e2a6daf (v2.3.2), but the fix never reached the widget's copy of this code until now.
  • Obfuscation plugin key exposure. obfuscate() used the published keyPrefix as its AES key. If keyPrefixLength was overridden, part or all of that key could be published. It now encrypts with the full derived key and publishes only half of it. With default options the output format is the same, so existing obfuscated strings still decode.

Fixes

  • SHA key derivation. Each round now hashes the full digest from the previous round, and the result is cut to keyLength once at the end. This is what altcha-lib and all server ports do. Before, the widget's solutions were rejected (invalidSolution) for SHA-384 or SHA-512 with cost > 1, and for any SHA-* challenge with keyLength below the digest size and cost > 1. The default (SHA-256, keyLength 32) was not affected.
  • PBKDF2 key length. PBKDF2/* now supports any keyLength. Before, only 16, 24 and 32 worked.
  • Algorithm names. The built-in deriveKey functions reject names they don't support. Before, unknown PBKDF2/* names fell back to SHA-256, and SCRYPT and ARGON2ID ignored the name. Each function now accepts only its own exact names:
    • SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512
    • PBKDF2/SHA-256, PBKDF2/SHA-384, PBKDF2/SHA-512
    • SCRYPT
    • ARGON2ID
  • Input validation (altcha/lib):
    • createChallenge checks cost, keyLength, memoryCost, parallelism, counter, counterMode, expiresAt, hmacAlgorithm and the secrets.
    • createChallenge also checks the key prefix. keyPrefix must be a non-empty hex string, and it is lowercased before signing. keyPrefixLength must be a positive integer smaller than the derived key.
    • verifySolution returns invalidSolution for a malformed derivedKey (it must be lowercase hex) or counter (it must be an integer the counter mode can encode), instead of throwing or coercing the value.
    • solveChallenge throws immediately on an invalid keyPrefix instead of running until the timeout.
    • hexToBuffer rejects non-hex characters.
    • Canonical JSON keeps a __proto__ key, so an injected key now breaks the signature.
    • verifyServerSignature:
      • checks payload.algorithm against SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512;
      • requires hmacSecret;
      • returns invalidSignature when the signature is missing;
      • checks expiry against the current time without rounding it down to whole seconds, so the up to 1 second of grace is gone.

Upgrade notes

Challenges that are already in flight with these settings will not verify across the upgrade.

  • Calls that used to work and now throw:
    • verifySolution without hmacSignatureSecret, or with an empty one.
    • createChallenge with hmacSignatureSecret: '' or null.
    • createChallenge with hmacKeySignatureSecret but no hmacSignatureSecret.
    • createChallenge with an empty or non-hex keyPrefix.
    • createChallenge with a keyPrefixLength that is not smaller than the derived key.
    • Any built-in deriveKey with an unsupported algorithm name.
Changelog

Sourced from altcha's changelog.

[3.3.0] - 2026-10-05

  • Fix: SHA key derivation hashes the full digest each round and truncates once, matching altcha-lib and the server ports (SHA-384/512 and any keyLength below the digest size with cost > 1 previously failed server verification)
  • Fix: PBKDF2 supports any keyLength (uses deriveBits instead of an AES-GCM key)
  • Fix: built-in deriveKey functions reject unsupported algorithm names
  • Fix: verifySolution requires the re-derived key to match the signed keyPrefix, rejects malformed derivedKey/counter values, and validates secrets and hmacAlgorithm
  • Fix: createChallenge validates its options (keyPrefixLength below the derived key length, non-empty hex keyPrefix lowercased before signing, positive integer cost/keyLength, valid counter and expiresAt)
  • Fix: solveChallenge fails fast on an invalid keyPrefix
  • Fix: hexToBuffer rejects non-hex input; canonical JSON keeps __proto__ keys
  • Fix: verifyServerSignature validates algorithm and hmacSecret, handles a missing signature, and uses exact expiry
  • Fix: obfuscation plugin encrypts with the full derived key instead of a keyPrefixLength-sized prefix

Updates `radix-ui` from 1.6.7 to 1.7.0
Changelog

Sourced from radix-ui's changelog.

1.7.0

Dialog

  • Fixed nested, portalled layers being unusable inside a modal layer. A non-modal popover rendered inside a modal Dialog previously broke some user interactions because the modal layer's trapped FocusScope reclaimed focus, and its RemoveScroll only allowed scrolling within the modal content.

Navigation Menu

  • Added a disableToggle prop to NavigationMenu.Sub.
    • true: Clicking the trigger of an already-open submenu item keeps it open. This is the default and matches existing behavior.
    • false: Clicking the trigger of a submenu item toggles it open or closed.
  • Added an activationMode prop to NavigationMenu.Root and NavigationMenu.Sub.
    • "automatic": Hovering or focusing a trigger opens its item, and moving away from the trigger closes it after a short delay. This is the default and matches existing behavior.
    • "manual": Pointer entry and focus never open an item. The item opens when its trigger is clicked.
    • When activationMode is omitted on NavigationMenu.Sub, it inherits the value from the parent NavigationMenu.Root, so setting "manual" on the root also applies to submenus unless a submenu opts back in to "automatic".
  • Fixed a bug where a submenu's defaultValue was reset when an external element was focused before the menu opened.
  • Fixed a bug where NavigationMenu.Viewport discarded its children and rendered the active content in their place. The active content is now rendered inside the consumer's element alongside any children it already had.

Popover

  • Added Popover.Title and Popover.Description parts that provide accessible names and descriptions for popover content.

Scroll Area

  • Added a ScrollArea.Content part so consumers can own the wrapper element implicitly rendered by ScrollArea.Viewport. Pass disableImplicitContentElement to the viewport and render ScrollArea.Content as its child.

    <ScrollArea.Root>
  <ScrollArea.Viewport disableImplicitContentElement>
    <ScrollArea.Content>{children}</ScrollArea.Content>
  </ScrollArea.Viewport>
  <ScrollArea.Scrollbar>
    <ScrollArea.Thumb />
  </ScrollArea.Scrollbar>
</ScrollArea.Root>

    In the next major release, the viewport will no longer render this element implicitly. We recommend migrating to this API now for a smoother upgrade.

  • Fixed a bug where asChild on ScrollArea.Viewport merged props onto the implicit content element instead of the consumer's element.

Slider

  • Added a preserveThumbOrder prop to Slider that prevents thumbs from crossing over one another. When enabled, each thumb is constrained to the values of its neighbors instead of swapping positions when dragged past them.

Other updates

  • Added support for multiple aria-describedby attributes, so id strings from a component and its child are merged, normalized, and deduplicated instead of one replacing the other.
  • Fixed a bug where internal event handlers were still called on disabled Select.Item elements.
  • Fixed a bug where a paused Toast would not auto-close after its duration changed while the timer was paused.

Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.63.0 to 1.64.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.64.0

🧰 WebMCP

New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });
const page = await browser.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com');

for (const tool of await page.webmcp.tools())
console.log(tool.name, tool.description);


const result = await page.webmcp.callTool('add', { a: 2, b: 40 });
console.log(result.content[0].text); // "42"

Playwright MCP also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as webmcp_<tool>. Pass --no-webmcp to opt out.

playwright-cli exposes them as well:

playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'

🎬 Better videos

Videos can now be recorded at a custom frame rate, and the decorations for actions are styled with plain CSS:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
use: {
video: {
mode: 'on',

fps: 60,

actions: {
style: {
point: 'width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 50%; background: red',
highlight: 'outline: 2px solid #333; background: rgba(0, 128, 255, .15)',
title: 'font-size: 16px',
},
},
},
},

Updates `@vitejs/plugin-react` from 6.1.1 to 6.1.2
Release notes

Sourced from @​vitejs/plugin-react's releases.

plugin-react@6.1.2

Fix HMR for compound components (#1484)

Adding or removing a component from a compound component was not handled, creating stale updates. Doing this now triggers hmr invalidate on the file and propagates the invalidation to importers.

Fix compiler.logDiagnostics option not working (#1483)

With oxc-transform-react >= 0.148, the logDiagnostics was not working. This version fixes it and requires oxc-transform-react >= 0.152 as a peer dependency if you are using the compiler option. compiler.logDiagnostics option is now deprecated and should be swapped for the builtin compiler.reportDiagnostics.

Disable refresh for non-jsx with compiler enabled (fix #1478) (#1485)

When the compiler was enabled, TS files could trigger fast refresh which would cause runtime errors. The logic now follows what the builtin oxc plugin in Vite does.

prs.title: fix: bound resolver cache invalidation scans during publication
prs.body:
## Product Updates

- [ ] Highlight
- [x] Other — Solution deployments spend less time refreshing source caches.
- [ ] Omit

## Summary

Solution publication invalidated each source module with a separate full Redis traversal for its name and each parent package. Publishing 75 Python files required 209 traversals; a measured production traversal took 6.073 seconds, putting this work alone beyond the 15-minute deployment deadline.

Scan the resolver cache once per source update, with COUNT 1000, and filter exact module/ancestor names locally. Preserve immediate invalidation across scopes and the existing deadline. This reduces repeated scans without changing cache ownership or import behavior.

Validation: 21 cache unit tests and 42 import-boundary, solution publication, and real Redis integration tests passed. API Pyright and Ruff passed. The Redis integration regression seeds 10,000 unrelated keys and verifies affected entries are removed while neighboring entries remain. Read-only production comparison found identical targets for the old and new selection behavior. Merged and deployed on October 13, 2026. The production CSP 0.1.21 retry succeeded in 87.72 seconds end to end (64.87 seconds for the server job), using the patched build-runner image. The main release workflow completed successfully, including rollout and API/client smoke.

Performance verification: the actual baseline and fixed module writers were run against isolated real Redis with 90,000 unrelated keys, 324 resolver keys and the CSP package's 75 Python paths. The baseline took 257.03 seconds and 1,824,465 SCAN requests; three fixed runs took 3.16, 4.39 and 5.08 seconds with 6,825 requests each. Completed runs verified invalidation across scopes and preservation of unrelated keys. This is 51–81× faster for cache publication, not a full-deployment timing guarantee. One baseline sample completed; redundant baseline repetitions were intentionally stopped, with cleanup confirmed. Fixed-only repetitions completed normally.

[Reproducible benchmark and production projection](https://github.com/gobifrost/bifrost/blob/codex/solution-publication-stall/docs/performance/2026-10-13-module-cache-invalidation.md). Benchmark Ruff lint/format checks passed; no production cache mutations were made.

Fixes #982

prs.title: Remove resolver scans, expire agent-step streams, and report publication phases
prs.body:
Solution source publication now invalidates resolver metadata without traversing Redis. Agent-step streams get a bounded lifetime, and the existing durable Solution job reports publication phases and storage timings.

This follows #982 and the now-merged #983. It is rebased onto current main; the immediate repair and its benchmark evidence remain separate. Jack authorized queueing this follow-up after #983 merges. No manual deployment or production cleanup is authorized.

Changes:
- Share per-name random generation tokens across scopes. Rotate exact names and ancestors transactionally, validate reads atomically in API and synchronous workers, and fence delayed cache writes. Expiring tokens/results avoid a persistent scope index. Metadata moves to a v2 namespace; module/import authorization and per-execution import snapshots retain their existing behavior.
- Commit XADD and a sliding 24-hour expiry together. Preserve terminal/delegated deletion and clean up exact streams after retention deletes AgentRun rows. Provide a bounded, aggregate-only, dry-run orphan inspector as a script and in manual retention previews; it performs no mutation.
- Report coarse monotonic publication phases through PlatformJob and aggregate elapsed time for S3, source-index, Redis, app upload, and activation. No deadline, transport, or polling change.
- Preserve #983’s exact/ancestor/cross-scope/unrelated-key regression contracts with zero-scan expectations. Update its reusable benchmark to check visible resolver results and clean owned generation tokens; its original branch/results remain untouched.

Architecture, source audit, operational cleanup recommendation, and exact verification commands: `docs/plans/2026-10-13-redis-invalidation-and-hygiene.md`.

One paired isolated benchmark (75 files, 90,000 unrelated keys, 324 scoped resolver entries): #983 took 3.0699 s / 6,825 SCAN requests; generations took 0.0411 s / zero scans. Both correctness checks passed; fixture cleanup left Redis DB 15 empty. This is one local cache-only sample, not full deployment or production latency. Raw results: `docs/performance/2026-10-13-resolver-generation-results.json`.

Rollout requires API, worker, and scheduler to move together after draining active executions/publications; mixed versions do not share the resolver generations. Old metadata expires within its existing 24-hour bound. Historical persistent streams are not retroactively expired. The orphan preview protects existing AgentRun rows, recent streams, invalid identities, and unknown types, and reports SCAN page truncation. Production cleanup requires a separate reviewed operation and explicit approval; no production keys have been deleted or flushed.

The proportionate audit records the persistent source-path index’s expired-member growth and remaining role/form/bulk-reset scans without changing unmeasured authorization-cache behavior.

Validation:
- Focused module/import/SDK, stream/retention, executor, publication, and source-index tests passed. The retained cross-process happy path starts one source-only deploy job; new edge cases use direct Redis/database services with zero extra jobs/builds.
- After rebasing onto merged #983/current main: 171 focused unit cases and 19 Redis/database/publication integration cases passed, with zero failures/errors/skips in JUnit. Earlier pipeline-mock corrections also passed 62 focused cases.
- API pyright and ruff passed. Product-update structural validation passed; final disposition validation is recorded in the plan.
- Preliminary CI ran 9,106 backend unit cases and caught two missed test/inventory updates. Both reproduced locally and were corrected: session tests model transaction buffering, and Redis inventory now detects/classifies Lua reads. Expanded local verification passed 136 cases before identifying two existing Lua owners; after their source-reviewed classification, all six final inventory/session cases passed. Full local backend/client/Playwright suites, `pre-pr`, and `pr-preflight` were not run. No client/public DTO changes, retries, skips, timeout increases, or warning filters.

## Product Updates

- [ ] Highlight
- [x] Other — Solution deployments refresh source caches faster and report publication progress.
- [ ] Omit

Canonical disposition: `product-updates/dispositions/pr-984.json` with approved review status and the queue authorization as evidence. Structural validation passed.

Queue validation exposed one E2E test assumption: a single SCAN MATCH page need not contain the fixture streams. The test now follows continuation cursors across 1,000 unrelated owned keys and requires an empty intermediate page, preserving non-deletion assertions. The failure reproduced locally before correction; all nine stream/retention integrations passed afterward. Production inspection remains one bounded page. Full queue validation will run again.

Configure the shared React editor loader with the installed Monaco ESM module and bundle its editor, JSON, CSS, HTML and TypeScript workers as same-origin Vite assets. Independently seed the table and document acceptance lifecycles so all persistence assertions fit their own browser budgets; update their ledger bindings.

Dashboard and desktop/mobile app editor journeys also assert no uncaught page errors. The unchanged production client reproduced the reported error boundary; the fixed production build passes that journey.

The existing startup configuration now loads bundled Monaco eagerly (~1.15 MB gzip); language workers are loaded on demand. No dependency or API contract changes.

prs.title: Protect privileged accounts and correct access-check behavior
prs.body:
Prevent account changes from removing the final active human Platform Admin, refuse privileged roles for external users, and improve run cancellation and Access Check attribution.

### 1. Last active Platform Admin

Shared account services refuse role removal, deactivation, and deletion with HTTP 409 when the change would leave no active human Platform Admin. A lock on the built-in role serializes concurrent removals before a fresh membership query. Identities do not satisfy the guard.

### 2. External users and privileged roles

External users cannot receive privileged additional or base roles, become external while holding privilege, or hold a role whose permissions are being elevated. Token minting preserves the account's external flag across password, MFA, SSO, MCP, and bridge paths.

### 3. Policy role membership and workflow powers

The compatibility expression `user.is_platform_admin` reads actual Platform Admin role membership at any boundary. Flags alone grant no policy authority. Policy-write permissions are privileged.

Canonical admin policy seeds use the existing role and workflow power model: Platform Admin role holders pass, and Full workflows retain their configured powers within the run user's reach. The existing platform default and workflow overrides still select Full or Restricted. Full adds no organizations; Restricted adds only its configured capabilities. The migration updates exact canonical seed nodes while preserving surrounding custom policies and arbitrary `user.is_platform_admin` expressions.

### 4. Reach for table and file policy routes

The report-only evaluator accepts a cross-organization table/file request when a role boundary covers its target, then leaves data access to the policy. Other non-permission classes keep their existing refusal. The live provider-organization paths remain registered for their later removal; no provider-organization policy is seeded.

### 5. Deleted users' unstarted runs

Deletion cancels durable Scheduled and Pending executions in the same transaction. Promotion refuses preserved lineage whose user has disappeared, and dispatch cannot overwrite a deletion-side cancellation. Redis-only queued work is cancelled before dispatch if its run user is gone.

Should deactivating a user also cancel their unstarted runs? This change preserves the existing deactivation behavior.

### 6. Agent attribution

Agent bridge Access Checks retain the acting user and direct attribution, add `surface: agent`, and include the agent run ID. Other request surfaces are preserved.

### 7. Temporary permission-pass samples

Direct non-admin people now record successful permission checks once per person, decision, and day. Platform Admins, identities, and runs do not produce these samples. The code marks this temporary observation behavior for removal at enforcement cutover.

### Rulings I made

- Lock the stable Platform Admin role before reading surviving people. Cost if wrong: account changes contend on one short transaction rather than allowing concurrent removals to invalidate each other's checks.
- Treat privileged custom base roles like additional roles for external-account protection. Cost if wrong: a role editor must remove external holders before adding privileged permissions.
- Migrate exact canonical admin seed nodes, including nodes inside edited policy documents; preserve custom predicates. Cost if wrong: a customized legacy predicate intentionally remains membership-based and may require its author to choose the workflow-power expression.
- Resolve workflow policy powers from the persisted execution and its workflow, using the configured default when appropriate. Attribution claims cannot supply powers. Cost if wrong: missing execution provenance grants no added workflow policy powers.
- Treat the atomic transition to Running as dispatch start. Cost if wrong: a run already claimed for dispatch can finish after its user is deleted; unclaimed and queued work is cancelled.

### Verification

Passed: `./test.sh quality api` (Pyright: no errors or warnings; Ruff: passed), client type checking and lint (five existing warnings), 72 focused client tests, 157 focused backend tests, and 51 account race/regression tests. The full backend unit result is recorded below.

./test.sh tests/unit/test_identity_authorization.py -q

prs.title: Zero Trust Automation: enforce current roles and reach
prs.body:
Zero Trust Automation checks the original user's current roles and organization reach across platform requests and durable runs. Full Access remains the workflow default; this does not convert workflows to Declared Permissions.

Depends on the merged preparation changes #992, #994 and #995.

## Resulting behavior

- Workflow, Agent and Service credentials identify durable records. Authentication reloads current authority rather than trusting permission or organization claims in a runtime token.
- Full Access adds all named permissions, including Secrets, inside the original user's reach. Declared Permissions adds only configured permission capabilities. Run As changes the acting identity and attribution; it adds no reach or authority.
- Platform operations check named permissions at persisted resource organizations. Collections filter reach before paging and counting; moves check both organizations. Table and file policies still decide data access after reach is established.
- App and Form launches use verified parent capabilities, and result reads remain bound to the accepted embed session. History, diagnostics, notifications and PlatformJob deliveries recheck current visibility.
- Services pin a run user per attempt. Missing historical bindings fail closed. Legacy placed workflow grants become permission-only capabilities and require renewed Solution consent.
- OAuth overrides and plaintext credentials require Secrets access. Child processes use authenticated runtime operations instead of Redis authority or deferred SDK writes.

## UX and terminology

**Zero Trust Automation** names the overall model in the security overview, runbook and Product Update. Workflow badges and access traces use **Full Access** and **Declared Permissions**; API/manifest values remain `full` and `restricted`. The reviewed Auditing tabs, compact record selector, drawer and Aggregate Off list are inherited from #994/#995.

The final integration repairs preserve tool-picker management access, bound Solution preview scope, metadata-only HMAC settings access, private-Agent budget controls, subscriptions after filtered events, and the HMAC form result route for its accepted embed session. Revocation still removes unauthorized deliveries, including individual file prefixes sharing a channel. MCP connection and knowledge document detail reads hide foreign rows before checking the persisted target. Service shutdown commits and closes the claim transaction before waiting for child completion, preventing a reproduced callback/database lock cycle.

## Upgrade and rulings

Drain active work and stop old producers/consumers before upgrading the API and workers. Prior runtime credential formats are rejected. No historical actor or permission binding is guessed. Review affected Solution permission requests again after normalization.

- Original reach stays independent of workflow powers and acting identity. Legitimate automation outside that reach needs an explicit role placement.
- Consumer sharing and data policies remain authoritative; management permission permits managing reachable workflows without granting new organization reach.
- Unbound historical work must be restarted with an accepted identity rather than reconstructed automatically.
- Renewed consent may require repeating an approval that was previously intended.

The deactivated-user cancellation proposal remains deferred; delete-time cancellation is preserved.

## Verification

- `./test.sh unit --tb=short`: **9,474 passed**, 53 existing slow tests deselected; zero failures, errors or skips; includes authorization, API inventory, DTO/CLI/MCP, generated-type, skill-truth, storage and import tripwires.

After this validation, the obsolete memory file was removed: its RSS field was absent, so its conditional assertions never ran. Batch shutdown remains covered by the service-owner-loss fixture and callback unit regression; ordinary success/failure worker execution has existing integration coverage.
- `./test.sh tests/unit/routers/test_websocket_table_messages.py tests/unit/test_solution_dev_proxy.py tests/e2e/platform/test_subscriptions.py tests/e2e/platform/test_solution_dev_context_e2e.py tests/e2e/api/test_integrations.py::TestIntegrationConfigSecrets tests/e2e/test_execution_logs_list_endpoint.py -v --tb=short --durations=0`: **61 passed**, no skips.

## Summary

Existing app bundles could receive a workflow-not-found response when an authorized user opened an app in a sealed Solution. Restore the user's app context for workflow resolution, table access, and file reads while retaining current user reach, app visibility, workflow sharing, and data policies.

App identifiers select context only. Runtime and embed credentials retain their existing provenance checks, and denied app contexts cannot fall through to a shared workflow with the same path. Header-based and older body-based SDK requests are covered without rebuilding apps or changing Solution settings.

## Validation

- `./test.sh quality api` — Pyright: zero errors/warnings; Ruff clean.
- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_solution_app_context.py tests/unit/test_spike_solution_param.py tests/unit/test_execute_solution_scope.py tests/unit/test_solution_dev_context.py tests/unit/test_solution_dev_adapters.py tests/unit/test_tables_sdk_solution_scope.py tests/unit/test_files_sdk_solution_scope.py tests/unit/sdk/test_sdk_workflow_execution_service.py tests/e2e/platform/test_sealed_app_user_context.py -v --tb=short --durations=10` — 150 passed.
- The new HTTP workflow regression fails with the ref-specific 404 before this patch and passes afterward. Global and org installs, current header and older body transports, sharing/reach denials, same-path shared-workflow isolation, table name/UUID policy, and file policy are covered.
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/platform/test_sealed_app_user_context.py -v --tb=short --durations=0` — 13 passed with the production managed-write guard explicitly enabled. Denied access is seeded during fixture creation, so the tests work independently of suite ordering.
- No deploy/build jobs are added by the new integration fixture. Deferred admissions are cleaned up before they become due. Integration call time is under one second; session user setup accounts for the longer setup time.
- Full backend/client/browser suites were not run locally; the merge queue remains the complete-suite gate. No client or API DTO changes.

## Product Updates

- [x] Other — Restore authorized users' workflow and data access from sealed Solution apps without rebuilding their apps.

prs.title: Fix app launch permissions for standard users
prs.body:
## Summary

Standard users could see an App but receive a 403 while opening it because the bundle manifest required `apps.read` (source inspection), although the built-in User role grants `apps.readbasic` for everyday App use. Load the manifest through the same canonical access check as runtime assets and update its access-list entry. Original-user reach, App sharing, source-reading permissions, and the existing write check for rebuilds remain enforced. No role grants or data migrations are changed.

App-loading failures now show a readable status-specific message instead of concatenating HTTP status and raw response JSON, including bundle preparation and standalone refresh paths.

## Validation

- Before the route fix, the new ordinary-user HTTP regression reproduced `403` with the permission-denied response. After the fix the targeted backend run passed 132 tests, including global/org standalone manifest and asset loading, source-read denial, sharing and foreign-org denials, stale legacy bundles without rebuild authority, and access-list enforcement/freshness.
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/platform/test_sealed_app_user_context.py tests/unit/routers/test_app_code_files.py tests/unit/routers/test_app_code_files_write_scope.py tests/unit/routers/test_application_authority.py tests/unit/test_access_list.py -v --tb=short --durations=0`
- The integration additions seed static dist directly and start no deploy, install, build, or worker jobs. Happy-path call time is approximately 1.2 seconds per case.
- `./test.sh quality api` — Pyright: zero errors/warnings; Ruff clean.
- `./test.sh client unit src/components/jsx-app/app-load-error.test.ts src/components/jsx-app/BundledAppShell.test.tsx src/components/jsx-app/StandaloneV2App.test.tsx` — 35 tests passed.
- `(cd client && npm run tsc)` passed. `(cd client && npm run lint)` passed with zero errors and one existing console warning in `client/e2e/support/seed-review-pack.ts:197`.
- Full backend, full client, and browser suites were not run locally. No API DTO changes or type regeneration are needed.

## Product Updates

- [x] Other — Restore standard users’ ability to open authorized Apps and show readable App-loading errors.

Release notes

Sourced from ossf/scorecard-action's releases.

v2.5.0

What's Changed

This release moves the action to Scorecard v5.6.0, the first Scorecard release since its hosted services moved to new infrastructure.

For changes to checks and results, and what the infrastructure move means for you, see the Scorecard v5.6.0 release notes.

  • The action's container image is built with Go 1.27.2 on a refreshed distroless base. by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1716
  • The installer (cmd/installer) now creates .github/workflows/scorecard.yml, and still recognizes existing scorecards.yml and scorecards-analysis.yml workflows. by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1716
  • The Scorecard version in results now always matches the Scorecard release the action is built with. by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1718
  • The action no longer prints the GitHub token variable while validating its options. by @​arpitjain099 in ossf/scorecard-action#1709
  • results_format accepts intoto, which wraps the JSON results in an in-toto attestation statement. by @​puerco in ossf/scorecard-action#1702

Other

  • Add a daily canary against Scorecard main by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1711
  • Bump Scorecard to the v5.6.0 candidate and fix the canary toolchain by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1714
  • Run Scorecard on every merge, add a zizmor presubmit, analyze workflows with CodeQL, and update RELEASE.md by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1716
  • Bump Scorecard to v5.6.0 by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1719

New Contributors

  • @​arpitjain099 made their first contribution in ossf/scorecard-action#1709
  • @​puerco made their first contribution in ossf/scorecard-action#1702

prs.title: List SDK integration mappings by Integrations Read reach
prs.body:
## Summary

Since #996, `integrations.list_mappings` in the SDK resolved one scope and then listed only that organization. A run with Everything reach (the provider Default Identity holds the Platform Admin wildcard role) therefore saw one mapping, and Global saw none. Scheduled fleet workflows, such as the organization directory sync and site, backup and mailbox refreshes, reported Success over a single organization. Authorization passed, but the data query discarded the caller's reach. The REST mapping list (`list_mappings_for_integration`) was already correct.

The SDK list now follows the same rule as the REST list:

- **No scope:** every mapping whose organization the caller may read with `integrations.read`. The filter runs in SQL through `permitted_organizations` / `OrgReach.where`, so role boundaries (organization, managed organizations, platform), Full Access and Declared Permissions behave exactly as they do for other reach-filtered lists.
- **Explicit organization UUID or `"global"`:** an exact filter inside that reach, with the existing reach and permission checks at that target. A scope never widens the result, and `"global"` now returns the Global mapping row instead of `[]`.
- **Caller with no reach:** 403, matching the REST list.

The SDK facade sends an omitted scope as unset instead of substituting the execution organization. No provider-organization or home-organization bypass is added. Per-mapping `secrets.read` redaction and external-caller config restrictions are unchanged.

**Hardening:** `get_mapping(scope="global", entity_id=...)` previously searched every organization's mappings after only a Global permission check. A Full Access workflow from any organization could therefore look up another organization's mapping, with entity and non-secret config. The lookup is now limited to the caller's `integrations.read` reach.

**Test harness:** a full local E2E run exposed two order-dependent tests, and both are fixed at the cause:

- **Live-LLM fixtures** (`llm_anthropic_configured`, `llm_openai_configured`) set the required `primary` and `chat_default` assignments to a live provider and never removed them. Later agent runs in the suite then called the live provider. The MCP gateway delegation test exceeded its 15s wait during provider retries. The fixtures now delete the rows they created; the API refuses to clear required assignments.
- **`test_scope_param_ignored_for_executions_list`** asserted a pre-RBAC contract. It passed only while org1 had no executions. It now asserts the documented contract: an explicit scope only narrows.

## Validation

- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_sdk_integration_mapping_reach.py`: 14 passed. Covers the Platform Admin role, managed organizations, an organization subset, home-only, platform boundary (Global only), no reach, Full Access, Declared Permissions with and without the grant, exact organization and Global scopes, a scope outside reach, and the reach-limited entity lookup.
- New E2E `TestScenario2a::test_platform_admin_lists_every_mapping_and_scope_stays_exact` passed; the existing worker-socket SDK parity test (`test_sdk_integrations_local.py`) passed.
- Full backend E2E run: 2337 passed, 2 failed. Both failures are the order-dependent tests above.
  - **Gateway test:** reproduced the leaked live provider (assignments and connections still present; the delegated run called `api.anthropic.com`). After the fixture fix, both are gone and the run made zero calls.
  - **Rerun:** after the fixes, the polluter followed by the two victim tests passed (16 passed).
- `./test.sh unit`: 9517 passed, including the DTO, contract-version and skill-truth tripwires. No DTO change.
- `./test.sh quality api`: Pyright with zero errors; Ruff clean.
- Client tests were not run because no client source changed.

## Product Updates

- [x] Other: workflows list every integration mapping their roles reach again, and entity lookups stay within that reach.

prs.title: Resolve table names through the org-then-Global cascade
prs.body:
## Product Updates

- [x] Other: workflows that use a Global table by name from an organization again read and write that table, instead of creating a private copy in the organization.

## Summary

Since #996, `get_table_or_404` required a table found **by name** to belong to exactly the requested scope. The SDK always sends the run's organization as `scope`, so a workspace workflow naming a Global table got 404 from an organization-scoped run. #996 kept the org-then-Global fallback only for Solution name lookups.

- **Reads** (`get`, `query`, `count`, `update`, `delete`) of Global tables returned 404 from organization runs.
- **`insert` and `upsert`** treated the 404 as "table does not exist" (`bifrost/tables.py` `_ensure_table_exists`). They created a same-name table in the customer's organization with the admin-only default policy and wrote there. After that, every lookup by that name in the organization resolved to the copy, and regular users were denied. In production this created 17 copies across 4 organizations in two days, including lifecycle `onboarding_runs` and the cache tables, so portal users saw "couldn't load the run".

**Fix:** names resolve through the canonical `OrgScopedRepository.get(name=...)` cascade, org then Global, the same as every other scoped entity in `api/src/repositories/README.md`.
- A scope only selects where the cascade starts. The cascade can return only the requested organization's table or the Global one, never another organization's.
- UUID lookups stay exact: an explicit scope must match the table's own organization.
- Original-user reach and each table's policies still decide access. This restores the pre-#996 resolution without adding authority.

Data already written into organization copies is not migrated by the platform. Each instance decides how to merge its own tables.

## Validation

- **New E2E** `TestDocumentScopeQueryParam::test_org_scoped_name_writes_cascade_to_the_global_table`: a regular user inserts, updates and reads by name with their own organization as `scope` against a Global-only table. Every operation lands in the Global table. Before the fix this reproduced the production 404 (`assert 404 == 201`).
- **New unit tests:** an ordinary name lookup with an explicit scope uses the cascade; a UUID lookup keeps the explicit scope.
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/platform/test_tables.py tests/e2e/platform/test_policies.py`: 65 passed.
- SDK, CLI and Solution table E2E plus org-scoping scenarios (`test_cli_tables`, `test_sdk_tables_local`, `test_sdk_tables_writes_local`, `test_solution_table_e2e`, `test_table_solution_cascade_gated`, `test_app_portable_refs`, `test_org_scoping_scenarios`): 40 passed.
- Table unit tests (`test_table_resolution_reach`, `test_table_document_writes_service`, `test_solution_app_context`, `test_table_bulk_upsert_route`): 43 passed.
- `./test.sh unit`: 9519 passed. `./test.sh quality api`: clean.
- The full backend E2E suite was not run locally; the merge queue runs it.

prs.title: List mappings ignores scope and returns everything in reach
prs.body:
## Product Updates

- [x] Other: `integrations.list_mappings` lists every mapping you can see again, whatever scope it is passed, so existing callers that passed `"global"` or the provider organization see their customers.

## Summary

`integrations.list_mappings` is the MSP finder. In 30 days of Covi production use, 93% of its 72,987 reaching runs were provider fleet and finder workflows. Every call site enumerates the full set, then filters by tenant or organization. No call site relies on the list being limited to one organization. Single-organization reads use `integrations.get(scope=org)` or `get_mapping(scope=org)`.

#1008 made a `scope` on the list an exact filter. That broke existing user code:

- **Documented `scope="global"`** (the old SDK docstring: "Pass 'global' … to list across all orgs explicitly") started returning only the Global row. The Docs IT Glue migration, for example, resolved no organizations.
- **`scope=<provider org>`** returned only the provider's own mapping.

The list now accepts `scope` for compatibility and ignores it:

- **It always returns every mapping the caller may read with Integrations Read**, the same reach filter as the REST mapping list. No scope value narrows or widens it, so a customer user still sees only their own organization.
- **Scope is no longer sent by the SDK.** The request DTO keeps the field, with an updated description, so older callers still validate.
- **Single-entity reads are unchanged:** `get_mapping`, `get`, config and the rest return exactly the scope you ask for.
- **No organization-based permission is added.**

## Validation

- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_sdk_integration_mapping_reach.py tests/unit/sdk/test_sdk_integrations_local.py tests/unit/sdk/test_sdk_integrations.py tests/unit/test_dto_flags.py tests/unit/test_contract_version.py`: 90 passed. The contract fingerprint was refreshed for the description-only change; `MIN_CLI_VERSION` is unchanged.
- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_org_scoping_enforcement.py tests/unit/sdk/test_sdk_post_retry_opt_in.py`: passed. The list handler is now an explicit, documented exemption from the scope-resolver tripwire.
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/api/test_org_scoping_scenarios.py tests/e2e/platform/test_sdk_integrations_local.py tests/e2e/api/test_integrations.py`: 70 passed.
  - A Platform Admin gets every mapping for `None`, `"global"`, the provider organization and a customer organization.
  - An org1 caller passing `scope=org2` sees no org2 mapping.

prs.title: Let Full Access runs satisfy legacy platform-admin policy rules
prs.body:
## Product Updates

- [x] Other: Full Access workflows can again use tables and files whose policies admit platform admins, even when the person running them is not one.

## Summary

Before Zero Trust Automation, every workflow SDK call was evaluated as the engine superuser. A table or file policy written with `{"user": "is_platform_admin"}` therefore admitted any workflow run, whoever started it. Direct calls by non-admins were refused.

- **#992** redefined the legacy term as Platform Admin role membership.
- **The authority migration** (`20261016_policy_authority`) converted only the exact canonical `admin_bypass` seed to `{"authority": "platform_admin"}`.
- **In Covi production about 306 tables, across ~40 variants, keep the legacy term.** That includes older seed wording such as "Platform admins bypass all checks". A non-admin's Full Access workflow on any of them was denied. For example, a Covi technician's Portal V2 onboarding form could not read Global `org_config` ("Access denied").

`resolve_user_field(user, "is_platform_admin")`, used by both the evaluator and the SQL compiler, now also holds when the run carries the platform-admin policy authority. Only Full Access workflow runs receive that authority. `{"authority": "platform_admin"}` resolves to the same fact.

- **A direct call by a non-admin** is still refused.
- **A Declared Permissions run without the authority** is still refused.
- **No role or user fact is changed:** the principal's `role_ids` and `is_superuser` are untouched.

This restores the pre-Zero Trust Automation outcome for workflows without bringing back the engine superuser.

## Summary

Keep resource discovery and editing controls consistent with the access already enforced by the server.

- Use one shared resource access resolver for Apps, Forms, and Agents. Lists, direct reads, and Home reuse its original-user reach, named permission, and sharing decisions. SDK, MCP, and runtime consumers retain their existing adapters to the same decision.

prs.title: Move files in a location: files.move and files.move_many
prs.body:
## Product Updates

- [x] Highlight — entry "Move Files in a Location" is added to this PR with its number after it opens.
- [ ] Other
- [ ] Omit

## Summary

Workflows can move files inside one non-workspace location (for example a Solution's `docs` location) without downloading them:

```python
final_path = await files.move("campus-a/plan.pdf", "campus-b/plan.pdf", location="docs")
results = await files.move_many(
    [{"source": "campus-a/a.pdf", "destination": "campus-b/a.pdf"}],
    location="docs",
    on_conflict="rename",  # default "error"
)
```

The CLI adds `bifrost files move SOURCE DESTINATION --location docs [--solution INSTALL] [--rename]`, backed by `POST /api/files/move` and `POST /api/files/move-many`.

- **One durable platform job per call.** Each call enqueues a `files.move` platform job (up to 500 items; the summed source and destination paths are at most 200,000 characters). Bytes are copied server-side, the file's metadata row moves with it so path-prefix file policies grant access at the new path, and the source is deleted only after the copy is verified. Single-part copies use a conditional copy; larger files use multipart copy with `IfNoneMatch` on completion (hence `aiobotocore>=2.15.0`).
- **Authorization at enqueue.** Each item needs `read` and `delete` on the source and `write` on the destination, evaluated through the canonical file-policy path with a request-scoped `FilePolicyEvalCache`. Denials are audited 403s per item. Items succeed or fail independently and `move_many` returns per-item results in request order.
- **Safe retries.** Marker metadata on the copy lets an interrupted job resume, adopt a copy whose source is already gone, or report an already-moved file as success. Cleanup deletes only a destination it can prove is its own copy, and a resumed copy is never deleted. Three consecutive storage failures stop the job with `storage_unavailable`; remaining items are `not_attempted`.
- **Cancellation** is allowed only while the job is still queued.
- **SDK errors.** `files.move` raises `FileMoveError` for an item failure; both calls raise `FileMoveJobError` (`.job_id`, `.code`, `.results`) when the job fails or is cancelled. The SDK waits up to 4 hours by default.
- **Docs.** `bifrost-build` skill reference "Move files" covers limits, error codes, recovery, residual risks, and deployment requirements (bucket credentials need `s3:ListBucket`; configure an `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` lifecycle rule). Generated appendices, the operation inventory, the access list, the contract fingerprint, and `v1.d.ts` are regenerated.

### Merging with Zero Trust Automation

This branch merges `main` (rather than rebasing) to resolve conflicts with #996 and related access work once:

- The move cache now plugs into `FilePolicyService.evaluate()` → `FilePolicyDecision` and also memoizes `enforced_policy_principal` per caller, which keeps its identity-keyed claim pre-resolution valid.
- `_record_policy` (`access_check_policies.py`) now loads the run user and workflow powers once per request through the collector's existing per-request `cache`, instead of once per decision. A 500-item move enqueue from a workflow took **13.5 s** with the per-decision loads and **2.4 s** with this change (the e2e budget is 10 s). This also applies to table-policy recording.
- A malformed scope on a move is 422, the same as the other file operations after #996.

## Validation

All tests ran on the isolated `./test.sh` stack only (`bifrost_test` database, `bifrost-test` bucket); nothing ran against a real environment.

- Focused set on the final merge: **450 passed** — every test file this branch adds or changes, plus `test_file_policy_service.py`, `test_access_check_policies.py`, `test_access_check_hooks.py`, `test_sdk_files.py`, `test_dto_flags.py`, and `test_skill_appendix_fresh.py`, including the e2e `tests/e2e/platform/test_files_move.py` (moves with access following the file, retry adopting an interrupted move, multipart copy against SeaweedFS, and a workflow-driven 500-item enqueue within budget). Cancel is covered by `file_move/test_job.py` (cancel while queued succeeds; cancel while running is refused) against the test database.
- `./test.sh quality api`: 0 errors, 0 warnings; Ruff passes.
- Client: `tsc -b` and ESLint pass; `npm run test` 3,819/3,820 (the one failure, a `Knowledge.test.tsx` timeout, passes on re-run). Production client CI build on the final merge (Node 26 `client-check-runner`): build, checks, and 602/602 Vitest files pass.
- `scripts/check_skill_mirrors.py` passes; the regenerated client types match.
- Full backend suite (`./test.sh all`) before the merge: 62 failures on this branch vs 61 on its merge base `fb840fcc3`. The 61 are the same tests on both (log-capture and ordering pollution). The extra one, `test_repeated_large_table_responses_keep_health_responsive`, is a health-probe timeout that passed 4/4 when run alone. The full suite was not re-run after the merge.

## Known limits

- Signed-URL uploads take no lock. An upload landing between cleanup's ownership check and its delete is still deleted. The docs list the related upload races.
- The ownership check relies on `x-amz-meta` marker values. A client using a presigned PUT could set them; AWS rejects unsigned metadata headers by default, and this has not been verified on SeaweedFS.
