prs.title: Keep idle worker control subscriptions connected
prs.body:
The API’s cancellation and pool-command Redis subscriptions disconnect roughly every five minutes while idle. Enable redis-py’s built-in 60-second health PINGs on their existing shared client so idle subscriptions stay active; preserve reconnect handling and error reporting. Readiness failures now log the failing dependency and exception class without credential-bearing exception messages. This identifies a future failure’s cause; it does not claim the intermittent readiness failure itself is resolved.

Validation: 18 focused listener and health tests passed, including actual Redis PING emission, PONG filtering, subsequent command delivery, disconnect recovery/cleanup, and secret-safe health logs. API pyright and Ruff passed. Astra reviewed the patch with no blocking findings. Full suites are deferred to the merge queue.

## Product Updates

- [x] Other — Keep idle worker control subscriptions connected and identify dependencies that fail readiness checks.

prs.title: Reduce repeated work in runtime SDK authentication
prs.body:
Runtime SDK requests reload complete execution payloads and repeat a workflow lookup while establishing current authority. Select only authority fields, reuse the freshly loaded workflow for permission loading, and load the actor's provider flag in the same query. Every request still refreshes live status, identities, roles, and grants; this adds no authorization cache.

A real-Postgres comparison against the deployed control, with 20 alternating fresh-session calls per variant and a 111 KiB execution payload, measured 10→8 SQL statements, 8.660→7.291 ms median CPU, and 12.740→10.787 ms median wall time. Authority/principal facts matched. These are resolver measurements, not a claim about total production workflow speed.

Validation:
- `BIFROST_SKIP_BUILD=1 BIFROST_TEST_IMAGE_TAG=bifrost-test-cdc103dd ./test.sh tests/unit/authorization -v` — 451 passed.
- Same environment, `./test.sh tests/e2e/platform/test_sdk_config_local.py tests/e2e/platform/test_sdk_tables_local.py tests/e2e/platform/test_solution_permission_runtime.py -v --durations=0` — 20 passed, including service identity and consent revocation.
- Same environment, `./test.sh tests/e2e/api/test_agent_run_as.py tests/e2e/api/test_access_check_attribution.py -v --durations=0` — 5 passed, including an agent workflow tool acting as the run-as user.
- Same environment, `./test.sh quality api` — Pyright and lint passed.
- Report-only local measurements: the control/candidate resolver comparison passed; 18 actual remote workflow jobs passed in each timing phase. Five warm samples per case: config body 107→89 ms, 20-log body 222→211 ms. Echo caller varied 90→109 ms; no engine-body change. Host load is uncontrolled.
- Astra reviewed the frozen six-file patch: no authorization blocker. The payload projection test covers fresh/expired rows; it does not claim to evict payloads already present in an existing identity map.

The complete backend/frontend suites are left to the native merge queue. No public DTO, schema, deployment resource, or allocator setting changes.

## Product Updates

- [x] Other — Reduce repeated database work when workflows, services, and agents authenticate SDK requests.
- [ ] Highlight
- [ ] Omit

This remains part of the authorized production performance spike; no tracking issue is being created.

prs.title: fix(workers): prelaunch warm lifetime handoffs
prs.body:
A warm worker reaching its six-hour lifetime stopped claiming before its replacement initialized. Production showed a 53-second start delay during this handoff.

Prelaunch the standard warm replacement within the existing startup window. A reserved, starting, or ready replacement counts toward the warm target; all Jobs continue to count against Max workers. Existing workers finish normally, and no settings or resource limits change.

Validation: 92 worker-pool tests passed against real PostgreSQL with a fake cluster; the five corrected boundary cases passed again; Dockerized pyright and Ruff passed. Astra reviewed the final patch. Coverage includes exact lead-window boundaries, replacement deduplication, short lifetimes, and the hard maximum. Natural six-hour turnover has not yet been observed with this patch; a pool configured with Max equal to its warm minimum has no overlap capacity.

Commands:
```
BIFROST_SKIP_BUILD=1 BIFROST_TEST_IMAGE_TAG=bifrost-test-cdc103dd ./test.sh tests/unit/services/worker_pool/test_worker_pool.py -v
BIFROST_SKIP_BUILD=1 BIFROST_TEST_IMAGE_TAG=bifrost-test-cdc103dd ./test.sh quality api
```
Broader suites are delegated to the merge queue.

Product Updates: Other — Keep a replacement worker warm before a worker reaches its lifetime limit.

prs.title: fix(executions): use durable dispatches for queue positions
prs.body:
## Summary

The workflow queue could report completed runs as pending: Redis queue-position writes raced PostgreSQL claims, and stale-entry cleanup only ran in the former local worker monitor. Read queue membership and order directly from durable PostgreSQL dispatches instead. Pending assigned work remains visible; sync and completed runs do not. Existing WebSocket notifications and the queue response contract are preserved, with the original queue timestamp now populated.

Cancellation locks the execution and commits before publishing its queue snapshot. Invalid execution status filters return 422 before a database enum error can abort the request. Test resets also remove the ephemeral containers’ anonymous volumes, preventing repeated local verification from filling the host disk.

## Validation

- 141 focused queue, lifecycle, cancellation, and queue endpoint tests passed.
- 74 access-list contract tests passed.
- 28 harness and execution-read/cancellation tests passed after adding explicit cleanup for committed fixtures and updating the anonymous-volume orchestration tripwire. The first broad CI run exposed the old command expectation (10,327 other backend tests passed); its cause is corrected, with no retries or skipped tests.
- 33 shared execution-read tests and 10 execution query-parameter endpoint tests passed; both invalid-status regression cases reproduced the database failure before the fix.
- API type/lint checks passed with zero errors or warnings. A controlled 48-execution local replay passed: clean versus 50 stale legacy Redis entries measured 1.494 versus 1.501 seconds median completion; all outputs matched and the candidate did not read or write the retired key. This is one local run, not a production latency guarantee.
- Full suites remain the merge queue’s gate; they were not rerun locally.

## Product Updates

- [x] Other — show only pending workflows in queue positions and reject invalid execution status filters clearly.

prs.title: fix(workers): wait for executor startup before publishing capacity
prs.body:
## Summary

A newly admitted remote worker could report a memory budget while still reconciling its physical routes. The upgrade controller treats a non-null budget as usable capacity, so it could drain the old worker before the replacement began claiming work. Keep startup liveness heartbeats running, but publish capacity only after executor setup finishes.

This preserves existing database fields, authorization, worker limits, and Kubernetes configuration. A measured budget remains available internally to construct admission and reconcile routes.

## Validation

- The blocked-startup regression reproduced the defect: heartbeats published a 2 GiB budget before setup completed.
- 37 focused Docker tests passed across worker startup, API/remote host consumers, and the existing null-budget replacement guard.
- The final event-driven regression passed and cleans up its runner on failure.
- API type checks and lint passed with zero errors/warnings. Astra’s final review found no blockers.
- Broader suites were not run locally; the merge queue is the complete-suite gate.

## Product Updates

prs.title: Release workflow request connections before waiting for execution
prs.body:
Synchronous workflow calls retain their request database transaction while waiting for execution results. With 16 simultaneous callers, a controlled local run exhausted the database pool: all 16 callers timed out while 12 PostgreSQL connections sat idle inside open transactions. Child SDK requests and result completion need database connections to finish those calls.

Release the request transaction after authorization, cache decisions, and dispatch metadata reads, before dispatch/result waiting. The three boundaries cover inline code, provider cache misses, and ordinary workflows. Scheduled requests and provider cache hits return before these boundaries. Pool sizes, authorization, container limits, and admission pacing are unchanged.

### Validation

Real-PostgreSQL regression coverage uses a size-one pool to assert zero checked-out request connections at dispatch and successfully runs an independent query. Cases cover sync and async workflows, a genuine transient provider cache miss, and inline code.

The local saturation comparison used one API at 1 CPU / 1 GiB and one worker at 2 CPU / 2 GiB. The shared cached image was later found to enable the unmerged allocator experiment; these are paired mechanism results in that runtime. Stock-image confirmation is in progress before deployment; CPU, RAM, and latency figures below are not production projections. Both arms used the same image, scheduler disabled, and a synthetic 3:1 SDK/echo workflow mix. Every successful response was checked, and execution status/timings were hydrated from PostgreSQL.

| Source | Callers | Outcome | Completed/sec in 20s | Caller p95 |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| main | 16 | 16 request timeouts | 0 | — |
| this patch | 16 | 170 successful executions, 0 errors | 7.70 | 2.28s |
| this patch | 32 | 181 successful executions, 0 errors | 7.45 | 4.40s |
| this patch | 64 | 215 successful executions, 0 errors | 7.55 | 8.20s |

At 16 callers, the patched arm had at most one sampled idle-in-transaction connection, age zero, with no OOM and negligible CPU throttling. API/worker usage averaged 0.78/0.60 cores. Throughput remains around 7.5–7.7 executions/sec as queue latency grows; workflow-body p95 remains 171–185ms. This establishes the local connection-lifetime repair. Production latency attribution still needs the production workload comparison.

Focused commands passed:

```bash
./test.sh tests/unit/sdk/test_sdk_workflow_session_release.py tests/unit/sdk/test_sdk_workflow_execution_service.py -v
# 59 passed
./test.sh tests/e2e/api/test_data_providers.py::TestDataProviderCreation::test_non_transient_data_provider_execution_is_tracked_and_bypasses_cache -v
# 1 passed
./test.sh quality api
# pyright and ruff passed
```

Local commands used the cached Docker image via BIFROST_SKIP_BUILD=1 and BIFROST_TEST_IMAGE_TAG=bifrost-test-cdc103dd. Broader suites are delegated to the merge queue.

### Product Updates

Other / fix: concurrent synchronous workflow calls release their request database connection before waiting for execution results. Approved canonical disposition: product-updates/dispositions/pr-1093.json.

prs.title: fix: preserve GitHub token validation errors
prs.body:
A GitHub REST rate-limit response (HTTP 403) currently tells the operator that their PAT is invalid. The API labels every GitHub failure as an invalid token, the imperative helper drops the API detail, and the settings page replaces it with generic advice.

Preserve GitHub's HTTP status and reason through the existing error detail, client helper, toast and inline token-field alert. Clear the inline error when the token is edited or validation restarts. Keep Bifrost's existing HTTP 400 status so GitHub 401 responses cannot be mistaken for an expired Bifrost session. Failed validation still does not save the token.

Fixes #1095

Validation against current upstream main `1fab1d0` in an isolated worktree on a dedicated Docker test VM:
- `./test.sh tests/unit/routers/test_github_token_validation.py tests/unit/services/test_github_api.py`: 94 passed, zero skips.
- `./test.sh client unit -- src/hooks/useGitHub.test.ts src/pages/settings/GitHub.test.tsx src/pages/settings/GitHubTokenField.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`: eight passed under Node 26. The added helper/settings regressions failed on the original code.
- `npm run tsc`, `npm run lint`, and `./test.sh quality api`: passed. ESLint retains one existing warning in an unchanged E2E support file.

The API response schema is unchanged. Tests use synthetic tokens and mocked GitHub calls; no real PAT or deployment is involved. The full merge-queue suites were not run locally. Disposable test resources were removed.

prs.title: Emit workflow.completed after successful executions
prs.body:
Successful workflows can now trigger follow-up automation through the built-in `workflow.completed` topic. Emit metadata only after the terminal result is committed and synchronous callers are notified; subscribers fetch results through existing execution access checks.

Direct self-subscriptions are recorded as skipped, while distinct workflows can chain. Built-in emission keeps the existing failure events’ best-effort semantics; multi-workflow cycles require subscription filters.

Closes #1097. Requested by @MTG-Thomas.

The new live path executes one source workflow and one subscriber; 4.80 seconds including setup/cleanup.
